Let's lead off with saying it's a great game, addicting, consequential, challenging, etc...
This review isn't really a review.  I'm not here to highlight whether or not you should or shouldn't get the game.  You obviously should.
After playing for a while I thought I'd fill in some informational gaps for new players who have a hard time breaking into the game and getting geared so they can actually enjoy not being killed every time they leave the ship.
Before I go any further :
If you're just picking up Roguelands, bookmark that site, you'll be using it a lot.
1 ) Character Creation.  Race/Uniform/Augment.  All three of which can alter your build in some fashion.  Check the wiki to see what you want and how you can unlock it.
2 ) Ultimate Weapons.  Search the wiki for this so you know what I'm talking about.  These will be the staple for your build.  Everything else should be built around whichever one you pick.
3 ) You're going to die quite a bit outright.  That isn't a problem, in fact, it's something you want to do because you won't get anything unlocked until after you die.  What you do want to do is try to clear at least one map before you die, dump all of your loot/rewards into your storage, then head back out.
4 ) Once you've accumulated a decent amount of monster loot, you want to head to the Emblem Forge in your ship.  Every stack of 10 or higher Monster Loot you want to use this on to turn them into Emblems.  You should then refer to the wiki and figure out the recipes for the gear you need.  You might have to opt out for things you don't necessarily want so you can push further into the maps and farm more efficiently.
5 ) Find your Ship Droids terminal in your ship, upgrade all of the droids to max as soon as you can.  This and farming Hollow Cavern are the only means of reliably obtaining World Fragments.   World Fragments are used to purchase Mystery Gifts ( That have a small chance of giving you 4th Age Armor/Helmets ), Wealth Trophies that are used to purchase Arena Tickets, Remembrance Tickets, certain armors/items in Old Earth, Ion Tickets so you can go to Mega City ( Place for you to add mods to your equipment, turn your crystals into Prisms, and evolve your items with said Prisms.  Also has some stalls with items, mods, combat chips, etc... ), and the Lightsworn Crystal ( item used to unlock a specific race ).
6 ) I'd strongly advise against going to Whisperwood or Demon's Rift until you're more adept.  Moloch and Caius are a stride above the rest of the bosses of the normal maps and there really isn't any warning to the difficulty between them besides being overwhelmed mid-fight by their enormous health pools and superior battle mechanics.
7 ) Once you've made it to the Molten Crag and you're farming reasonably through the maps,  try heading back to the ship and using the computer to upgrade the Challenge Lv. of the map for tougher enemies / better rewards.  You won't start getting any mods for your gear outside of getting a random one here and there when talking to Shroomknight Wallace in Shroomtown until you start doing Challenge Lv. 1 or higher.
8 ) Probably should've came earlier in the list but if curiosity hasn't made you do so already, you might wanna' take a gander through that doorway in  your ship.  There are a lot of NPC's through there.  There's also a trash vendor/NPC that you can go to, to destroy any items you don't want and get some credits in return.  Those pesky cards that mobs drop all the time are a decent source of revenue.  There's also another doorway in this room that will take you to Captain Atlas and Lenny, in case you happened across the quest item and had no idea where to take it.
9 ) In between every hostile map there is a peaceful map with stalls that have various loot/emblems/combat chips/mods you can choose to buy.  There is also a quest-giver on this map that you shouldn't overlook.  The quests aren't generally that hard and some of them can give you good stuff.  Yellow quests will give you gift boxes similar to the ones you can buy in your ship with World Fragments except instead of 4th Age armor pieces they have a chance to give you a 4th Age weapon instead.
10 ) Probably the most valuable tip I can give you for starting out... Before you make the character you want to actually try to win with, make two others first.  As soon as you spawn in, put their resource farming Droid in your storage and then go kill them off.   Take those 2 extra droids and equip them to your real character.  You can now harvest 3 resources simultaneously instead of waiting on your one droid to finish a resource before it can start on the next.
Alright, I've imparted what little wisdom I have of the game so far.
Good luck, fellow meatbags.
Let's hope you have better luck than I've had.

Tera is by far the best MMO that I have experienced playing. While this is far from a new title, it continues to offer new content through regular patch updates.
Unlike many MMOs which offer generic "click and do damage" abilities with no real level of skill, Tera is mostly skill-shot based which greatly expands the skill cap for all of the players. To me a perfect game is easy to get in to and nearly impossible to master and that is exactly what Tera is. There is always something to progress towards without feeling overly grindy.
The world is expansive, visually amazing and filled with unique events to keep you entertained. Updates occur frequently so new dungeons are somewhat frequent.
Tera however is an older game with an older game engine which leaves for a few drawbacks.
• Optimization is poor, 30 fps is average on a mid/upper computer and 60 fps is virtually unheard of with good graphics.
• This game can be 'grindy.' The best gear is extremely hard to get and takes weeks, even months of continual play to get.
• Population is lower than it should be for a game like this. Queues for battlegrounds and dungeons can sometimes take a while.
• Leveling to 65 (max level) is a chore and completely worthless. Essentially it is a very long tutorial that could be shortened dramatically.
The game is great, fun, challenging and always expanding. Honestly, the biggest downside is that the population of this game is pretty low considering how good it really is.

Mindless fun...
It is mindless fun in a way. The cut scenes, done with awful animations by todays standards, is still something to giggle at. There is this scene where an englishman and italian chat  about tea while everything around them is shot to pieces.
The combat though, is far from nifty. In fact it doesn't pay when you avoid of the scripted path.
Example:  at the Tobruk scenario I decided not to persue the main objective directly, instead I took a left hook, attacked the enemy from the rear, taking his bases before proceeding towards the first main objective.
This resulted in me being punished for it. When I did take the first main objective it immediatly said I did the second and third main objective too and that ended the scenario, thus i was never able to accomplish the secret and optional objectives.
In all i missed out on 150 prestige points which is equal to 25 percentage of the points for the scenario.
Otherwise the game is hampered by a lot of issues. For instance, all cannon have the same effect. So an artillery pieces do more damage to a tank than a tank or tank destoyer do. You are relying heavily on repair and resupply units. Infantry is next to useless except for ai run mortar crews. The ai has lots of them and while mortars are next to useless against tanks in ww2 reality, in this game they are a deadly threat simply because there are so many around.
Recon units seem to perform good or bad depending on the side you play. Mostly they recon just about enough to let you see an enemy before they see you. It seems that german units are slightly favored.
Scenarios range from neat to annoying. You gain points with each scenario so you can buy better units, but not every scenario you are allows you to arrange your troops and spent the points you gained. A lot of them just throw you in with whatever the scenario gives and hits you at once with assault.
As said.. it is fun.. but you better of buying it on the cheap.

Overall the game does have some things going for it, the art style is interesting, minimalistic but pleasing, the Whole vibe of the game is well implemented and it has decent voice acting. However, the gameplay is plodding and repetitive, and it gives no way to accelerate past the repetition. Eg. Each day you get up, read the newspapers, start your crappy car (takes 3 times each time) and then pick an album to set the mood for the day. Now the first few times this really sets the mood nicely. Though, after a week or two of in-game time the fact you have to click the same damn spots and pick from the same too short tracks gets bloody annoying and you can't skip any of it. Maybe this was an intentional choice (to make you feel ground down and depressed just like the main character), maybe it just is bad design, in either case there is no good reason for it to be there or to keep playing after more than an hour or two unless you really like slow, plodding, facebook-like clicky games.

After playing around 60 hours I can say this is a great Assassins Creed game.
First off let me start by saying I'm playing on a fourth gen i5 4690k and a GTX1060 6GB on High and some settings Very High and the game runs smoothly. Barely ever get dips below 50, and I can even bump up my games resolution to 120% and still get an average of 51 FPS. My CPU usage hovers around 80-90% which isn't exactly normal but it doesn't seem to hinder my performance in any way. If you have a much newer CPU with more than four cores and a high end NVIDIA graphics card and new drivers you'll be fine performance wise. I hear AMD users are having lots of trouble with running the game smoothly, and players with four core CPU's are getting 100% CPU usage from the game.
The story is really good. Much better than Syndicates and Unity. It had some really great moments that had me very interested. Bayek is a very likeable character, his voice actor did a great job as well. Especially in some of the cutscenes. Overall most of the voice acting was really good. I did happen to find that some NPC's had what seemed like one singular voice line that would constantly loop, but it wasn't too many of them.
What's pretty cool is that I thought I was really stretching out my playtime, fitting lots of sidequests in between while doing treasure hunts and fortresses. After completing the final Main Quest I noticed how much there was that I STILL hadn't done. Including regions I didn't even explore. I was happy I had plenty to do after my story was complete, but my advice with this game is to really take your time and get everything done in each area as you go along. The side quests are enjoyable, and so are the other activites sprinked around the map.
The scale of this Assassins Creed is unparalleled by any other game in the series. The map feels massive, and every region feels and looks different and are all very fun to explore. I got a Witcher vibe from this game at times, due to the fact that I loved trekking my way to each objective on foot or with my mount without fast traveling because I loved exploring the areas so much.
I kept an open mind about the new control scheme, and it took me a bit to get used to but it didn't end up being a problem at all about 1-2 hours into the game. I noticed a lot of people complaining about the new controls, and I saw in the games hints and tips that you can bind any two keys to an action. So if you REALLY want your SHIFT+E and SHIFT+C instead of just ALT and C, then you can.
The combat is the one thing I WISH was done just a bit better. First I'll start by saying that it feels a lot better than it looks. Watching combat gameplay before I bought the game almost completely set me off. It looked flat-choppy-and boring. Though after buying the game, I came to the conclusion that it's just flat. Fights aren't really that intense, enemies can be taken out farely quickly with the correct combos. Yet somehow it still entertains me. Maybe it's the fact that you always look like a total bada$$ during combat. Either way, I'm still getting good fun out of it. The weapons are diverse and can be used differently in many types of situations.
The photo mode is addicting, if you couldn't tell by the amount of screenshots I've taken in game over the past few days. There are just so many moments in the game where you just have to get a great screenshot, its a truly beautiful game.
I'm still getting gameplay out of this game so I'd say it's totally worth the price. A big step in the right direction for the Assassins Creed Series.

On the surface Streets of Rogue seems like a mixture of GTAIII, Deus Ex, with the graphics of the original Zelda series, but what makes the game truly stand out is the fantastic and hilarious game play.  The game has unlimited possibilities and opportunities, which gives you endless ways to attack each mission.  Each level is randomly generated so you will never play the same level more then once.  I was giving an Alpha edition to review so all the missions that I was given were randomly generated without any actual story line to follow.  Story line or “Big Quests”, as they are called in the game are going to be appearing at a later date, which makes the depth of the game at this early stage in development that much more impressive!
The staggering number of options that you have at your disposal is one of the major aspects of this game.  Items that you can pick up and use, the ridiculous ways you can approach a mission and the many different ways you can interact with your environment, give this game a depth and replayability that is often not seen in Indie games. The other critical aspect of the Streets of Rogue is the emergent nature of the game play.  This is because of the fantastic AI characters.  They all act on their own, which creates many different situations for you.  The way they interact with the player, the environment and other AI characters leads to truly hysterical moments.  Streets of Rogue has done an incredible job combining both of these elements which leads to an amazing game with endless situations and endless game play.  You have so many different ways to approach each situations and every one of them is challenging, and most importantly loads of fun

streets of rogue
At it’s core, the goals of the game are pretty simple: On each floor, you are given 2 to 3 missions. These appear on your map screen, and there are a variety of different objectives that each mission can be comprised of. Each floor is almost like a small town, with a variety of different buildings filled with all sorts of things, and each individual mission will always be given it’s own building. Once you’ve completed the required missions, you can then access the elevator that takes you to the next floor. Each mission also gives you a variety of possible rewards, and some floors will contain a character that can offer you a totally optional mission as well.
Missions differ in how they work, including ones that have the same objective.  For example lets say your current mission involves neutralizing a character.  The character could be inside of a well protected building with guards, cameras, and trip mines or he could simply be a shop owner and just be sitting behind his desk.  Your first thought would be that the shop owner is an easy kill, but he probably has a high powered shotgun at his disposal, as well as other thugs in the store.  You blow up the walls and come in that way, or you could use stealth or maybe even become a vampire and bite him from behind.  The opportunities are endless. Your schemes will not always work out. There are loads of people in this bizarre city, each with their own agenda, and they can often screw up your plans in ways that you never expected, bringing you new troubles and causing chaos, adding to the emergent nature of the game play in a very dynamic and fun way. And you have tons of different ways of interacting with all these characters. Hire some goons to do your dirty work, or even bribe the cops on the current floor to ignore your crimes for awhile, among tons of other options.
When all else fails, pure combat is the only answer!  Thankfully, the shooting/combat system in Streets of Rogue is fantastic.  You move your player with the keyboard while the mouse acts as your aiming sights.  This concept gives you versatility while running away or strafing your enemies, while still allowing you to fire back from any angle.  There are numerous melee weapons to use.  The normal ones are there such as punch, knife, and bat, but you can also come across battle axs, swords, police batons and many more insane weapons. The same can be said about all the guns in the game there is a huge variety of guns and most are way over the top!  You also have the ability of using grenades, land mines and other explosives.  These explosives add aspect to the missions because they allows you to blow up most walls, giving you straight path to your objective.

You gain XP for completing missions and many other things.  Gaining XP allows you to give your character a new trait.  These traits give your player different abilities ranging from paying less at the store, to making ugly faces during combat which ends up scaring your enemies.  You can also activate mutators that change the game in a huge way.  These range from having very low health to other crazy ideas like no ammo.
The character selection is very diverse in the game and allows you many options.  You could play as a soldier, who has extra health and many guns or you could play as a doctor who isn’t allowed to use weapons. My favorite character is Dracula, his signature trait allows you the ability of biting other characters to regain health.  Each character has a different feel to them and changes your approaching significantly.  Fortunately they are all a blast to play with and it truly shows the creativity of the developers.
Streets of Rogue is a fantastic game that I would highly recommend. It is currently available thru Steam early access and I very excited to see what other amazing features the devs come up with!

Mini Ninjas is an adventure platformer which tells the story of six little ninjas on their quest to save the world. The story is very simple and linear but don't be afraid, it will bring you quite a lot to explore and tons of fun.
The game is kind of a mix of the Zelda and Mario games with cuteness and a leveling system. The player cuts their way through dozens of environments to reach the Castles on the end of each world where they have to defeat the evil samurai bosses.
Basically Mini Ninjas brings beautifully designed environments with great music, sounds and voice acting. It's really nothing new in this game, but its so fun, so cute and so lovely that you'll sure love it.

If you like ninjas, animals, cute things, and insanely beautiful natural environments, you'll probably like Mini Ninjas. It's a platformer/hack 'n slash with a surprisingly large variety of attacks, special abilities and playable characters.
The art style is like a sushi buffet for the eyes. It doesn't let story get in the way of simple ninja-versus-army-of-samurai action. However, its greatest flaw is the lack of any real challenge. All enemies and bosses are weak and predictable, and your team of YAANGU NIINJYA start out with everything they need to kick butt, then proceed to get crazy overpowered. By the end of the game your main ninja pal learns some ninjutsu that kills everything in the area.
If you play it, go into it expecting a charming experience, not a legitimate challenge. Basically a "casual action game". Whatever the heck that means.

Mini Ninjas is an extremely unnoticed game, and I believe it won't let you down. The setting is simple: A samurai warlord created an army by turning adorable animals into little warriors with his evil magic. The protagonists' mission is to defeat him and restore the balance of nature. Each character has his/ her unique abilities and special moves. Plus there are a lot of Kuji spells, potions and weapons so you can develop your own tactics to fight off the enemies. Besides, there are various scenes which are stunning and refreshing. You can fish, look for herbs and new Kuji spells while exploring.
The boss fights are incredibly fun as they have different weaknesses and you have to find out the specific tricks yourself to defeat them. The soundtracks composed by Japanese traditional instruments work flawlessly and suit the gameplay very well. The rhythmic Taiko Drumming adds so much tension.
However, the length of this game might be too short for those who have no interest in exploring and collecting stuff. The game might not work well in newer systems (because this is a rather old game)
To conclude, Mini Ninjas provided me an unforgettable gaming experience. I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes relaxing gameplay and imaginative stories.

Roguelands and Magicite are pretty similar in 2 ways. You can jump & dash, and you can level up. Otherwise, they are comletely different games. The crafting system is more complecated, having rare items actually does something towards what your stats are. If you've played Magicite and liked it, you will like this game. It may be a little grind-y at first, but it gets less so. A key feature is the multiplayer. See, it actually works! Magicite's multiplayer didn't work too well, but this one works like a charm! Anyways, it's basically like if a run in Magicite didn't end. Also, you get to hand-pick your traits, not roll them. :steamsalty:

After playing Magicite for so long, a friend introduced and bought me this game, and it's a very refreshing take on what may have been the same thing Magicite would have been. But instead, we got a new take on the style of game with a whole new background and even storylines to follow, as opposed to jumping right in with Magicite, with no context.
The crafting is very new as well, giving us a simpler (yet more confusing at times) method of crafting what you need.
Also, you have a storage! No more "Oh crap I died with all of my stuff! Dammit!" Instead you can store what you need and use it for your next characters. I'm assuming that because there is an ironman mode (no storage use ever on that character), that Sean will be kind enough to roll out even more modes that will make the game even more fun.
Pick this game up if you really enjoy side-scrolling roguelikes, especially if you're a space nerd like me. :)

. This would cause the global average surface temperature on Earth to vary by +/-2C within the same year which I'm guessing is enough to cause massive destruction from violent weather.

This is a brilliantly designed game.  As you progress through the murder mystery environment, you are left always wondering: What happened here? and Who is to blame?
The game never answers these questions.  It leaves you to decide how the story ended.  This is the best part.  You can never be wrong, and you decide what happened based on the evidence you uncover.  The developers don't want there to be a diffinitive, "Correct" story, so that each individual can decide and interperet from the events what the story is.
The other big seller for this game is after you complete the game, you can share your interpretation of the story on their website, and then read other people's experiences and stories.  You'll probably spend an extra hour or two seeing how other people interpreted from what you saw and didn't see along the way.
For just $3, this game is completely worth what you pay, and provides an experience that stretches beyond the 1 hour - 90 minute gameplay time.

See how many hours I have on this game? Yeah, enough said. Buuuuuuuuuut, since I love this game so much, I'll talk about it, anyway!
The outfits can be a bit showy and unrealistic, but it is a fantasy game, afterall. The characters, despite their lack of realism, have all their own personality and backstory, which ties in with what they need help with. This even applies to side-quest NPC's that you'll likely only be able to have a conversation with once!
Speaking of stories, Tera has a great one! The plot gets you into this nerdy RPG mode, if y'know what I mean. There may be a few jokes here and there, but it's still an action-packed, dramatic, lore-filled game!
If you have a weak PC, Tera's got you covered. Just go to the graphic options and you'll see a checkbox for low-performance PC's! It helps a lot with lagging, as well. Yet, the graphics won't become unbearable, mainly because the overall style of the game is just gorgeous! There's a lot of other options for your graphics, even if you do turn on the graphical dimming. So, don't worry! If you want lower quality grass and a beautiful sky, you've got it!
This is definitely not a pay to win type of game, so expect to work and spend time to complete quests. You can pay for things like accessories and faster mounts, but otherwise, it's play to win!
Oh, and did I mention that the combat system is the best I've ever experienced in an MMO? They have aiming, combos, and even gamepad support! It makes the gameplay adaptive to you! No more point-and-click bullcrap!
If all this doesn't get you started, then, well... maybe you should go back to clicking on enemies and watching your character kill them for you.

I bought this game during the autumn sale 2017, when year 2-operation 3 was about to end.  I got the starter edition at a discount as i was unsure of the game. I have had 90hr+ playtime till now(Dec, 2017).
pros:
1) base gameplay is very stable and good, you will never get bored of it. The game play is tactical and strategic having different gameplay choices.
2) tons of content released every year with frequent  updates. Maps are added for free with new operators, skins and has room for customization.
3) Each operator is  unique and well balanced. I haven't tried all of them but they are fun to play.They all have unique weapons and gadgets which are the most interesting part of the game, ie. playing with different ops and combinations of weapons and gadgets.
4) As i bought the starter edition i have to very few ops to start with and have to unlock others gradually by playing the game more and more.(this is a pro as i will explain in the next point)
5) the starter edition according to me is actually good. The game unlike other fps has a high learning curve and you need to know a lot before you start to win matches so the starter edition forces you to play the game more and more to unlock new ops and the more you play the better you get. If anyone bought the standard edition with the season pass and all he would have had everything from beginning which spoils the sense of accomplishment and also you will not learn anything about the tactical side of the gameplay. Hence i recommend you to buy the starter edition if you are  ok with getting to know the game thoroughly before jumping into online action.
6) my ping is actually quite good and rarely have faced connection issues.
7) runs well on even low end devices and is quite optimized for pc.
8) has a single player campaign to teach the basics of gameplay
cons:
1) matchmaking is not the best.
2) i have found the community to be so-so. Sometimes people are nice, sometimes they are rude.
3) the operator cost if were a little bit lower ot would have been nice. Skins and operators sometimes cost the same which is unreasonable.
Final opinion is i recommend the game to people who like fps games and also to those who are new to fps.. the game is tough to learn but gets interesting the more you play. You will not get bored of it easily. Gameplay is tight and tactical. Overall a very nice experience. If tou are skeptical to buy the starter edition, dont be.

* I take down the big mafia who has terrorized the city for generations. I get paid and the mission is complete. And then... nothing. Absolutely noithing. Nothing saying that I saved the city. Nothing giving me any hero status. Not anything opposite either, no-one comes for vengence. The only noticable effect is that I can no longer ask the mafia to perform any services.

If you're lucky, maybe City Hall will cut funding for one police officer. If you're really lucky.
* Speaking of which, later in the game, a character laments the city and the fact that it "attacks unarmed feminists with brute force". THAT DID NOT HAPPEN! I didn't do that, and yet the game assumes that I indeed blindely followed the story. It expected me to give in to the pressure (what pressure?) and do it.
* The personal storyline just don't make sense. Why doesn't Jack react when I gathered his half-million? Who knocked me down? Why don't I get to investigate who knocked me down? What point exactly does the mayor's-r*pe-victim-turned-lawyer-character play in the story? And what about the joint that is presented in the intro? Where does that come in? The entire story is just a bunch of loose ends thrown at you, and every time you HOPE that it will be something good and intruiging, but no. Not even his style-changes affect gameplay or storyline the slightest.
* Illusion of free choice is EVERYWHERE! I've played the game twice and actively made differing choices. NOTHING! Police promises to be a management/strategy simulator about the every day endeavors of a semi-corrupt police captain who is, naturally, a (period of time) away from retirement. The mafia practically owns his staff, his partner is implicit in some serious crimes, and city hall is run by a narcissistic maniac. The way this effects the story, and your consequences, is more shallow than it would like you to believe. While managing the day to day meta-map elements is entertaining, it quickly becomes a chore, and the game continues to drip feed you elements and tips/tools well into 3 hours deep. The game itself, with an unchanging game loop, is well over 19 hours long to complete I hear.
My frustration with Police is how heavily it corners you into doing what it wants. Why it couldn't be a linear story is anyones guess, but the design team gives you the option to do what you want, but the problem is, good cop gets you killed. Gotta be bad cop, or neutral evil cop, to progress any more than 3 hours into the game before it unavoidably kills you and autosaves while it does so.
Rating: 2.5/5 - Worth it for $10 or less, has a very polished presentation and unique story that captivates a certain element lost in most management games. Pigeon holing the players into doing what it wants, while lying about being an open experience, is frustrating to say the least.
Pros:
*Music selection is excellent, and unique. In-game purchasable albums and catalogs of music can be physically rotated at will. Neat.
*Roleplaying elements with your staff is cool and it's rewarding to see your best succeed.
*Tense, terse, focused and challenging from the get-go.
Cons:
*So many choices don't matter because they wind up getting you killed. Ultimately you need to toe the line until "it" happens about 15 hours in, and then you get one of two choices that actually do matter.
*Staff management and skill numbers seems arbitrary. When I can hire a 1500 cop, but they say something 1/3rd of that is "average", why can't this one cop do the job of three men? RNG seems entirely based off number of cops and not skill of cops. I've thwarted bank robberies with five old women and no SWAT. My best Sgt's get mowed down in a parking lot with one shooter, and no CYOA prompts to help me decide the outcome.
*Lack of sandbox mode until you suffer through and complete the entire thing.

Keeping with the happy reviews as another indie game I have played, has not dissapointed. Home is a short, pixelated, side scrolling horror game, which is based heavily on reading and exploration. Given the details mentioned this game is surely not for everyone, but putting that aside, why is it good?
Home is a very atmospheric game, giving players just ambience to listen to throughout the 1 hour long experience (I use this word instead of game on purpose), the story follows a man who has woken up in a strange, unkown place, and is set the main obkective of returning home, to find his wife. As you get closer to home the story delves deeper and more questions arise, finding strange objects and horrifying scenarios, but maintaining zero jump scares.
Home was enjoyable to play, being a game I could start and finish in one sitting, but as stated earlier there is no really exciting gameplay, but more of a filmic experience. I give Home 6/10

Like the similarly named Gone Home or even The Stanley Parable, Home is an experience that may challenge your definition of what a game really is. And like those other two games, I think Home is probably best played without any expectations or prior knowledge about the game or what it is. Having said that, you should probably stop reading this if you haven't played Home and think you might want to. Just know that you should play it if you like narrative focused games or unique, thought provoking experiences. Also it's really short and probably best played in one sitting, so set aside an hour or two and play Home. And Gone Home. And The Stanley Parable. If you haven't already.
Still reading eh? I'll try not to spoil too much of this game then. In Home, your character wakes up in an unfamiliar house with blood on his clothes and an injured leg. He can't remember what he was doing before or how he wound up in the house. He soon finds a dead body and makes other unsettling discoveries which prompt him to want to race home as quickly as possible to make sure his wife is okay. Along the way, you'll find clues that may offer insight as to what your character was doing before he blacked out or why he wound up in that house to begin with. You'll also need to make some decisions that will affect how the game plays out. For example, you find a live rat stuck in a mousetrap: do you free him or leave him be?
Graphically, Home is pretty simple. Standard indie game pixel art graphics. But I think the graphic style suits the game perfectly. Home and Lone Survivor are a good demonstration of how when you have a simpler graphic style, the sound and music design becomes more impactful. The player is paying more attention to what they're hearing to as opposed to what they're seeing. I don't think Home had superb sound design, but it was a good example of less is more. Most of the time, you'll just hear the player character's footsteps and maybe the occasional background noise which are adequate to create the atmosphere. But when you hear something unexpected, it can be very surprising or unsettling. I did have a few control issues with the game though. On several occasions, I accidentally skipped some text that I was still reading and the game wouldn't repeat the text or go back to it. And the game felt a bit unresponsive sometimes when playing with a controller, but these are minor complaints.
Okay, past this point is spoiler territory. The ending of this game warrants some discussion because it's what makes the game unique and interesting. But I don't think I can dance around the ending without revealing it, so if you don't want the game spoiled, stop reading.
The game does a good job of creating suspense and setting you up with mysteries like "Who killed the man in the house? What was your character doing in that house? Where is your wife? Is she alive or dead? Are you the murderer?". Depending on your actions and decisions, you'll get clues that can support theories about the answers to these questions. But the game will not directly give you any sort of concrete ending. It's left vague and up to the player's interpretation of the clues and events to draw conclusions about them. In fact, at the end Home, the game will link you to its homepage (ha ha) where you can see other player's interpretations of the game's events and share your own. I was initially kind of put off by this. I think I was expecting the kind of ending that 999 had where there's a great twist at the end, the player is given satisfying answers to all of the mysteries of the game, and all of your questions are explained and wrapped up. Nothing like that here. After being initially dissapointed, I decided to play through Home again since it's only an hour or so long. I found I enjoyed it more the second time where I could focus on the details and try to form my own viewpoints on the game's ending.
Home certainly isn't for everyone, but I love this style of game. I love games that tell me a good story or can make me stop and think a bit about what the game was trying to communicate. I hear Benjamin Rivers is now working on what is being described as a "futuristic sci-fi psychological romance" game. Sounds completely crazy, and I'd like to play it

Ever been to the movies, to watch something you normally wouldn't watch, and at the end said "Hold up, I need to gather my thoughts."?
Home is an open ended game that, in all aspects, works like a movie. Gameplay seems to be just a linear exploration and interacting with stuff that gets highlighted. You are then prompted for your thoughts on some interactions. You say whatever you want/think about it from the given options.
You basically are fed ambiguous information that your mind tries to decrypt. You always have the same basic path to reach the same end-point. And you always have to make one fundamental choice.
Without giving any spoiler, since this game is all about the experience, the ending ruins everything. Not because there is an ending, but because basically you answer some relevant questions and are given an akward explanation that goes with whatever you answered. This is crucially flawed, in my opinion, since "every run will be different", but not by much: there's one critical event at the very end that is foreshadowed throught the irreversible middle-sections that the narrator uses to conveniently sum up the important things you perceived, and the rest is pretty much meaningless. The ambience is pretty much all this game has going in its favour.
Should you pick up the knife on the floor, covered with what appears to be blood? It depends on your current view about yourself, a guy that seems to know very little about himself. Does freeing the rat from the rat trap in any way change the outcome of it all? I don't know, and I don't care enough to find out. Is it that the list of girls you run into twice mean that you murdered them? You can see where this is going. You, the player, are the one that is putting meaning into the things you find. The one and only thing I was curious about while playing the game was
, but even that isn't enough to make me want to go through playing the game again. The reason I have 2.1 hours on record is also because when I first played the game there was no autosave mechanism implemented and had to quit at about 40 minutes in because of stuff in the real world; the game is that short.
Also, I don't consider this to be a major spoiler, but Home is absolutely titled the way it is because a) you find yourself initially in someone else's, and b) you end the game at yours.
The game has a metascore of 69 out of 100: I guess it's a fair value. I personally got Home at a big discount, and I'd advise you to do the same if you really want to play it. If you want something with a little more gameplay and can handle the horror genre, try Lone Survivor since it's an overall better investment.

Disclaimer: I was not a fan of previous AC games, I didn't hate them but was on the fence every time I played. I have never been drawn to the series. I decided to give AC:O a chance as I liked that it now includes loot based itemization and levelling.
AC:O features a lot to do, but with a poor control/combat system and a boring story so far as I have played it. I don't believe I'll put much more time into this game and if I do, I may end up changing my review.
I would say that if you haven't been a fan of the AC series so far, don't bother with this one.
Pros:
- Good graphics (typical Ubisoft graphics)
- Beautiful surroundings, great atmosphere
- Ton of quests/things to do
Cons:
- Clunky controls, tried both Xbox controller and M/KB. Both are clunky and have their own drawbacks.
- Combat. I am a fan of Dark Souls combat, Witcher 3 combat I can stand. The combat in AC:O is a mish mash of both, but fails to do either well.
- Terrible and/or annoying AI. I've run face first into enemies before without even triggering them to see me. Enemies will chase you forever on horseback and are frustrating to take down as they'll run away shooting you with arrows. On the flip side, if you just kite enemies forever it feels like you can never die as health regenerates in combat, which leads to long drawn out, boring fights.
- Boring story that goes nowhere fast. Just seems insulting to be asked to play hide and seek with kids.
- Poor frames, running on 980ti, i7-7700k, 32gb DDR4 ram, m2 ssd
- Overwhelming amount of quests at some points that usually cause me to shut off the game.

The story sinks you down in the mood and then melts your heart.

This is one of the best Assassin Creed game ever made and i give it 9/10. Why not Full point ? Here is some problems.
* Some of the quests have several parts and a middle part is sometimes clearly taken out.
* Several weapons can be bought for real money only. If i could get them by solving riddles or quests i would be ok if i
could skip that and just buy them, but when i pay full price for a game, i want to have access to ALL the content, without paying more.
* I have really liked the historical facts in all AC games, buildings, individual and events. about 5% of that is left in this game.
* Multiplayer have always been a weak part in the AC games, but here is none at all. ( well, revenge quest for a fallen player you never met or cared about... )
* The main story have very litttle to do with the AC series, you could have also called it Uncharted: Origins or Tombraider : Origins with very little changes.
* You meet many friends and allies along the way, and all will not survive this dangerous period of time - i would have liked some more time with the ones that didn´t make it. Now it is just another face that appear and is gone within an hour,  simetimes less time than that.
* Microtransactions and Denuvo.... really ? * spits after getting a bad taste in my mouth *
* Really expensive game if you want ALL the content.
Now to the good parts:
* Very fun game with about 80 hours of varied and interesting gameplay.
* Beautiful nature and graphics, the people that worked on clothes, weapons, vegetation and especially water have done an amazing job. The water looks very different depending if is close to a city, desert, swamp or very deep. I think no other game have done water this good.
* Moving, riding, fighting and climbing is very natural and fluid. ( i play with xbox control. )
* The difficoulty level is very slowly increasing, and i really like that. ( some might complain that it is to easy even on hard... )
* The photo ability is a nice touch, i have taken more pictures than i dare to admit.
* The basic version of the game give you a really nice time for a fair price ( 50 Euros on amazon for well over 50 hours of gameplay, that is fair in my eyes... )
In the end, recommended game - 9/10

The game is decent, but not great by any stretch of the imagination.  I own copies of AC1, AC2, AC Revelations, AC Brotherhood, and AC4 Black Flag along with this game, and I've played through 1, 2, Revelations, and now 3.  I've also played a large portion of Black Flag.  Out of the whole group that I've played, this one is by far the lowest quality AC game I've ever played.
A lot of people don't like Connor, and I can understand that, but I don't really have a problem with him given that Altair in the first game had just as bad an attitude as Connor does.  My main problem with this game is gameplay mechanics.  The controls are simpler than previous AC games, but I still have a lot of problems with Connor doing a right-angle turn and climbing a wall when I need him to run straight ahead, and that gets really old really fast, especially with the massive amount of guards you have to deal with in this game as compared to previous franchise titles.
Some of the missions had requirements that I didn't know about until I got desynced, usually having to do with being detected or not killing anyone.  I don't know why Ubisoft felt it necessary to not let you know in advance what the mission requirements were before entering the fray.
The story is okay, though it's a lot more self-righteous and preachy than I've seen in past installments.  I've played some of Black Flag and I find that the preachiness has been heavily subdued, something I am very happy for.  I really don't like Connor's consistency when it comes to his naivety.  He is naive all the way through the game from beginning to end, and that lack of development really bugs me.
The biggest complaint I have is that I bought the Deluxe Edition with several of the DLC's included, and I can't play any of the DLC's that came with the game.  Even though I have activated all the keys in Uplay, the game insists that I have to enter the keys again, and when I do, I get the dreaded "Invalid key" error message.  I've been wracking my brain and looking all over the place for a solution to this problem.  Seriously, I am considering pirating this game just so I can play the DLC's that I have already paid for and which Uplay says are all activated and ready to play, because the game itself won't acknowledge that the DLC's have been activated.
So I cannot recommend this game.  I am grateful that I got it on sale for under $10.00, because if I had paid full price for this game, I would be much more upset than I am now.  Great way to ruin your reputation even further, Ubisoft.  Maybe next time you want to fight piracy, try removing your oppressive DRM from games that people have actually bought from you.  After all, the only thing your DRM does at this point is punish paying customers for buying your stuff.  If you hate piracy so much, then please, by all that's holy in your books, stop encouraging piracy with your DRM that keeps honest people from being able to play the games that they bought from you with their own money.

Hey guys, thank you for reading this. I'm triing to keep this veage and short so as not to keep any of you away from the game for too long. So let it begin ...
On the good side:
The story is magnificently epic. It makes not one point about our society, how it twists ideals for it to benefitial, or that in the end we are not so different, just have different points of view, and I could go on...
The main character, Connor, is an extremely compelling person, especially when you see this pure hearted, naive, but dedicated man interact with the stealing, cheating and lying world that came to be around him and react to the ways they eventually try to use him for the greedy goals some people have.
This game is beautiful. I could almost feel the smells of revolutionary America. The world feels alive along with the chatacters. Their costumes are authentic (maybe Connor the exeption, but Assassins alway stood out) and the faces are rendered very well. You can see all of their emotions right id front of you.
LOADS of things to do. From the ever popular assasin contracts trough liberatable forts, to the new naval missions line, the side content is entertaining, especially the latter mentioned part. The ships handles very well and there are plenty of upgrades to pour the hard earned ingame money to.
The bad side (not dark, becouse that is cool and has cookies):
The combat is just too ... f*ckin ... easy. Minimal tactics required. I literally NEVER managed to die in combat, even with like 20 people cruising around me. I get that Connor is a beast, but that's just too much. Spamming counter attack will solve all of your problems, period.
Bugs are all over the place. And I'm not talking about the ingame mosqitoes. Dead soldiers stuck in the air, randing npc' spawning right in front of you ... I'll let you explore the rest.
The brotherhood system, oooooh yes they implemented that as well, is completely unnecessery, albeit it can be useful with all kinds of skills theese trainees unlock, but still, the entierity of the game is more than completable without them.
And there you go people. I left out a couple of thing, like crafting becouse I have absolutely no problem with it, in fact I enjoyed it very much, but don't think of it as something that must be mentioned above.
I hope you will have as much of a good time with this game, as I did. It's my favourite AC title so far and it will take a while for me to get bored of it.
Thank you for reading and have a good time mates!

Cosmic DJ is a musical, rhythmic gaming experience.  The story is kooky,
but irrelevant.  The game is about building and creating your own music. There
isn't a score system, and no real failure state; instead the game is about laying
down a "sick" beat and melody.  You are limited to what tones are provided to you,
which limits  the player from creating something truly unique to the player.  It
missed the mark a bit there, because the mechanics to provide this are there, they
just don't allow more freedom to the player.
One fun feature is the availability to use the music any way you want, with
no copyright issues, you can download it onto your computer to listen to at your
leisure.  For the price point, this game is easy to recommend.  It is simplistic
yet goofy and fun, even if its a little short.

A good game with a nice mix of progress and risk. The combat takes a little bit to get used to, but for most people it shouldn't take too much effort to become acquainted. At this point, the game is still being regularly updated, so I can't call out a lack of content, and even today there's still far more than $10 worth of material to play through. I don't really mind the permadeath aspect, as it adds a level of risk to the game, but I do oppose the idea that dying is necessary for unlocks. This system worked well in magicite because there was actually a game to finish, meaning you could live through an entire playthrough and then recieve your unlocks. Here, you could spend hours on a character, finish all the content, yet never die due to care and practice. However, if you want to unlock those races, augments and costumes (which can add massive bonuses/alter gameplay entirely) you need to literally purposefully die. Of course you can stash all your gear and what not and then die naked, but you still lose the levels and expensive♥♥♥♥♥end game combat chips. Though many rogue-like aspects fit well into this hybrid game, unlocks by death do not.
Apart from that, the game is top-notch in my opinion with it really shining in multiplayer (with some bugs). With a few more updates (maybe some level design changes to spice things up) this game can only get better.

UPDATE After 21 hours I just finished this game today and would like to edit and update my previous review. Feel free to have a read. Spoilers are at the very end and should be tagged.
Originally I stopped at day 161 at about hour 15 because I found the game unfun and very repetitive.
This game can be quite addicting and engrossing as you get quite involved in the characters and the plot that unfolds.
In short this is a police dispatch simulator not that different from 911 operator. You have to make decisions on what police to send to a 911 call based on a few lines of information.
What makes this different from 911 operator is of course you only work with police, you don’t assign equipment (like xcom) and all dispatch is from only one central location. One thing that makes this better is a better is there is a lot more human element with police making excuses not to turn up, characters asking for police favours and of course much stronger story.

Overall.
I enjoyed the graphic style and the voice acting in the unravelling plot. I also appreciated the story despite it been predictable but there is so much quiet time you have to tap out and spread out this game.
Yes I was invested in the characters, I felt for Jack Boyd and his problems and was personally frightened at the way he was acting and treating the people around him.
As you progress through the game you are given a few more powers (and have some taken away) which can sometimes come in handy. Admittedly I don’t remember ever using the party options given as I was focused entirely on the money goal and almost always felt understaffed.
Day to day events
The daily excuses from the police trying to miss shifts are interesting at first and make me wonder whether or not I should write some down to see if the same police are repeating themselves.
Oddly enough I don’t see an easy way to build up a case against an officer to fire them later.
For example I'm sure somebody had their father die twice. However they just becoming annoying after a while.
I lost count how many times I've just said no to 5 people in front of you. Tell me why would I say yes to you to READ A BOOK!?!? Is reading a book more important than making sure that your fellow officers or members of the public DON'T DIE today?
The investigation solving isn't too bad as they are usually fairly logical and give you a nice break from the daily responding and dispatching. There are a few times when it can get a bit maddening as you are certain every piece is where it should be and it's not letting you advance. It feels like getting a password wrong by one capital letter.
Once in awhile when your police respond to a call there are some nice jokes mixed in between
Of course I will instruct my officer to unzip themselves and urinate on a fire.
A lot of the normal part of the game is a bit punishing and annoying.
One big gripe was the punishment you get from the Mayor who really doesn’t like you.
What is the logic of punishing the police for underperforming by removing police positions?
How on earth will that improve response times or performance? This just feels simply too ridiculous not to call out.
Yes I understand that they have to put you in financial stress to further the plot as it would be too easy to be a straight laced cop if you didn’t have these pressures.
I feel that this title game suffers from the same problems as 911 operator and Beat cop and This war of mine. There are all very anchored in the reality of the setting and real time. However I see too much realism and not enough ...game.
Yes the settings for all these games are all dark so I can’t entirely blame this design.
As I wrote in my original review, do not play this in as few sittings as possible. Try to break it up into several play sessions over a week and several weeks of a year.
I played this right after Beat cop and 911 operator so was personally interested in continuing the theme.

This Is the Police has some good ideas, managing cops in a corrupt and morally bankrupt town sounds like it has so much room for great character interaction and enthralling storytelling. Unfortunately, it fails at almost every avenue. First off, some positive points, because there are some - It's a game with undeniable style and high quality visuals, music and UI. That about names everything I can say are consistently great in this game.
My gripes include the following -
Character interactions are so laughably negative. At first, I thought "wow this game is pretty depressing and nihilistic", but when every character is a bad guy... what reason do I have to keep caring? It makes EVERY single plot point and character predictable. If you want to create a world that's macabre, grim and morally bankrupt, you don't make every single character that! It doesn't make it more depressing, it just makes it comical. Like, oh wow! Another bad thing happened, that's REALLY surprising this time. That hasn't happened the last 100 times. I'm not even asking for a world that's more believable. I'm asking for a story where morality isn't so binary. It isn't disturbing that all these bad things are happening, because it's all I've come to expect.
You've not made me care about this world, it's clearly broken beyond repair - Why am I meant to be upset? Why am I meant to suddenly care? I can't get invested in these characters because none of them deserve any better, they're literally all just sponges of negativity that say edgy, inflammatory remarks. Having moral bankrupt characters is good, it's obviously what you'd hope for in a game about crime, but not every character has to be this way. I've never seen such negative and disturbing themes done so laughably. You're never taught to expect anything but negativity, betrayal, and immorality. If you want to just read "bad things that can happen, bad things that people can say", then oh boy you are in for a treat. I wanted a story where there are good characters that have to make difficult, unethical decisions for a greater good, or in hopes of a greater good. This is like driving off a bridge and picking up a kid as you're about to plummet into the water, and then you live and nobody finds out so you go to the kid's funeral and♥♥♥♥♥♥on his grave. And you♥♥♥♥♥♥on his parent's doormat. And then you wake up the next day and do it all over again, for the next 3 months with different kids. That's the kinda moral system we got in this game, that's the kind of characters you're meant to... somehow empathise with, or care about, because the gameplay is fine but pretty repetitive and the little bits of story and dialogue you get inbetween is CERTAINLY not well-written or engaging.
This is genuinely one of the worst stories for an idea that is SO good in theory. There's attention to detail spattered around the crime scenes you go to, and I really like that. But every time the story continues on, I physically can't stand it. If there was more focus on the crime scenes and their little stories and interactions, I think I would've enjoyed this game a lot more. But with how focused it is on its main story and characters, which are so unrelentingly awful... it's painful. Oh the mayor is telling you to fire black people again, then the next day says on the news that he doesn't know why the police force doesn't have black people. Oh he's complaining about gay people now. Oh, gotta hire some asian people to make some Japanese guy happy. Oh, someone's boyfriend just reported a♥♥♥♥♥♥on her... Turns out she's actually cheating on him. Oh, the main character is gonna see his wife and mend their relationship! A glimpse of hope! Nah, sorry he's been knocked out and in a coma. Now I get to speak to the press about what happened, oh I got 4 negative choices to make... hm, which one do I pick - it's quite difficult, I really don't know which way to be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a game full of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, I'm sure there's no way I can compete.
Welp, I think I enjoyed the absurdity of This is the Police more than I could ever enjoy its self-involved, morally devoid world for any longer. I love nihilistic and depressing stories but this is just plain awful storytelling and dialogue. Please don't homogenize your characters to this extent. In a world of unrelenting negativity, at least give a semblance of hope, even if it's false. I want to have a reason to play, other than "more bad things happen in bad world. Pretty bad, hey?"
3.5/10 I like the concept and art style. It's a technically well made game design wise but the story is honestly one of the worst I have encountered in any medium, be it film or video games or otherwise.

I bought this game on a sale for 49 cents when my steam wallet was down to less than $1 and I didn't feel like adding more funds to it.
Gameplay is repetitive and gets old very fast. Within 15 minutes I had been exposed to 95% of the content in the game and I was already tired of it. The pseudo-retro graphics are very well done and refined however; that coupled with a pretty nice chiptune soundtrack makes it a relatively well-put-together game. The stealth idea is alright, but the levels seem to be for the most part hard-coded and there is very little randomness to the game other than the location of loot and the key. If you get caught, you lose all of your money and things and are forced to start over again (Not 'forced' per se; all of the levels you have unlocked remain unlocked under the condition that you lose the equipment required to complete the level. For instance, if you get caught during Level 3 [which contains a dog and laser tripwires], you've now lost your lockpick and dog decoy causing you to have to repeat levels 1 and 2 to earn enough money to buy another lockpick/decoy).
There are better flash games than this, but if you buy it on sale it's probably not that bad.

Disclaimer: I was not a fan of previous AC games, I didn't hate them but was on the fence every time I played. I have never been drawn to the series. I decided to give AC:O a chance as I liked that it now includes loot based itemization and levelling.
AC:O features a lot to do, but with a poor control/combat system and a boring story so far as I have played it. I don't believe I'll put much more time into this game and if I do, I may end up changing my review.
I would say that if you haven't been a fan of the AC series so far, don't bother with this one.
Pros:
- Good graphics (typical Ubisoft graphics)
- Beautiful surroundings, great atmosphere
- Ton of quests/things to do
Cons:
- Clunky controls, tried both Xbox controller and M/KB. Both are clunky and have their own drawbacks.
- Combat. I am a fan of Dark Souls combat, Witcher 3 combat I can stand. The combat in AC:O is a mish mash of both, but fails to do either well.
- Terrible and/or annoying AI. I've run face first into enemies before without even triggering them to see me. Enemies will chase you forever on horseback and are frustrating to take down as they'll run away shooting you with arrows. On the flip side, if you just kite enemies forever it feels like you can never die as health regenerates in combat, which leads to long drawn out, boring fights.
- Boring story that goes nowhere fast. Just seems insulting to be asked to play hide and seek with kids.
- Poor frames, running on 980ti, i7-7700k, 32gb DDR4 ram, m2 ssd
- Overwhelming amount of quests at some points that usually cause me to shut off the game.

This is one of the best Assassin Creed game ever made and i give it 9/10. Why not Full point ? Here is some problems.
* Some of the quests have several parts and a middle part is sometimes clearly taken out.
* Several weapons can be bought for real money only. If i could get them by solving riddles or quests i would be ok if i
could skip that and just buy them, but when i pay full price for a game, i want to have access to ALL the content, without paying more.
* I have really liked the historical facts in all AC games, buildings, individual and events. about 5% of that is left in this game.
* Multiplayer have always been a weak part in the AC games, but here is none at all. ( well, revenge quest for a fallen player you never met or cared about... )
* The main story have very litttle to do with the AC series, you could have also called it Uncharted: Origins or Tombraider : Origins with very little changes.
* You meet many friends and allies along the way, and all will not survive this dangerous period of time - i would have liked some more time with the ones that didn´t make it. Now it is just another face that appear and is gone within an hour,  simetimes less time than that.
* Microtransactions and Denuvo.... really ? * spits after getting a bad taste in my mouth *
* Really expensive game if you want ALL the content.
Now to the good parts:
* Very fun game with about 80 hours of varied and interesting gameplay.

S Y N O P S I S:
Cosmic DJ is a short romp through a wild story about keeping the good vibes flowing through electronic music. Its gameplay revolves around 'jamming' to a preset back track and layering instruments and melodies to move onto the next stage. Don't expect much flexibility in terms of music creation. All the tracks are set to a specific key signature, measure, and tempo. There is also a limited number of instruments to play with for each track; all of which are set to a specific chord progression. These limitations, however, don't detract from the simple fun of jamming along and freestyling the sequence of melodies and instruments. The story is humorous and engaging enough for players to plow through the short 1 hour plot (give or take a few minutes depending on how much the player extends each jam session). Some players may think this is too short without enough content. I'd say that the length of the game is appropriate for the context of this title. The experience will leave a smile on your face once it's through and you'll wish there was more. Luckily, there is some replayability in a Quickplay mode that lets you choose sets of instruments to jam with and create new tunes. One of the best features of the game is its ability to export your jam sessions to MP3s, complete with cover art that you make within the game itself, using the various crazy visuals and stickers they provide. All in all, this is a great indie title for anyone who enjoys rhythm games and quirky, offbeat humor with pop art visuals. Give it a shot!

This game is short, sweet, and for those itching to make a quick beat.
Gameplay wise, this game will have you dishing out beats using many different instruments. I find it delightful when I make a beat that just sounds pretty damn good, and if you enjoy what you made, you have the option to save the music so you can listen to it later. Also, the number of levels are few, but each are fun and offer a unique style that would most likely intrigue you, whether it be the rocket corgis or the flailing puppets.
Moving on to what I have to say about the graphics, I must say, they are charming and I enjoy the retro feel of it all. The game is bright and colorful, and the levels offer different styles to keep things wacky and strange, which I enjoy about this game. It's quirkiness and humor is enjoyable.
The audio, oh, the audio. Being that this is a rhythm game, the music features catchy techno tunes that will have you bobbing your head as you create your music. Also, the narrator, a funky shaped fellow, has an... how should I say... enticing voice.
Overall, this is a game that should be played if you enjoy music, want to create it, and want to experience the quirky world that is Cosmic DJ. Considering the low price, this game is well worth trying.

Hot dang this is a cool game. I didn't understand what it was at all before buying, but it's definitely up my alley.
Basically, you're thrown into a level with several missions (rescue this person, kill this person, retrieve this item), and they can be completed however you see fit. Literally any way you want to. If you want to be a soldier, you can just shoot everyone on the level. If you want to be a ninja, you can sneak past people and backstab targets. My favorite is the shapeshifter who can change to be anyone they see.
Each level is filled with different NPCs of different roles, and the AI is fairly sophisticated (at least, it's better than I expected). If you are a gangster, watch out for rival gang members. You can speak to friendly gang members and recruit them. If you're a thief, shopkeepers will be hostile to you. If you're a crazy naked guy, literally everyone hates you. For good reason.
All this means you have to navigate the level, and constantly assess your environment to see how you want to achieve whatever it is you want to achieve. There are tons of items to help you do this (from EMP grenades to teleporters to a simple crowbar), acquired either through theft, murder, barter, or mission completion.
The game also has a lot of humor and doesn't take itself too seriously.
Definitely a lot of fun, and I'll keep this in my Steam favorites for play every once in a while.
NOTE: This game is not completed. There are only 2 zones to go through (I believe there's supposed to be 3 for the base story). From what I can tell, the developer is pretty solid, but this Is an early access review after all. I'd recommend you buy it on sale if you're a penny pincher, as it's not something that you can play all day every day. But I definitely recommend getting it at some point if it seems like it's up your alley.

This Is the Police has some good ideas, managing cops in a corrupt and morally bankrupt town sounds like it has so much room for great character interaction and enthralling storytelling. Unfortunately, it fails at almost every avenue. First off, some positive points, because there are some - It's a game with undeniable style and high quality visuals, music and UI. That about names everything I can say are consistently great in this game.
My gripes include the following -
Character interactions are so laughably negative. At first, I thought "wow this game is pretty depressing and nihilistic", but when every character is a bad guy... what reason do I have to keep caring? It makes EVERY single plot point and character predictable. If you want to create a world that's macabre, grim and morally bankrupt, you don't make every single character that! It doesn't make it more depressing, it just makes it comical. Like, oh wow! Another bad thing happened, that's REALLY surprising this time. That hasn't happened the last 100 times. I'm not even asking for a world that's more believable. I'm asking for a story where morality isn't so binary. It isn't disturbing that all these bad things are happening, because it's all I've come to expect.
You've not made me care about this world, it's clearly broken beyond repair - Why am I meant to be upset? Why am I meant to suddenly care? I can't get invested in these characters because none of them deserve any better, they're literally all just sponges of negativity that say edgy, inflammatory remarks. Having moral bankrupt characters is good, it's obviously what you'd hope for in a game about crime, but not every character has to be this way. I've never seen such negative and disturbing themes done so laughably. You're never taught to expect anything but negativity, betrayal, and immorality. If you want to just read "bad things that can happen, bad things that people can say", then oh boy you are in for a treat. I wanted a story where there are good characters that have to make difficult, unethical decisions for a greater good, or in hopes of a greater good. This is like driving off a bridge and picking up a kid as you're about to plummet into the water, and then you live and nobody finds out so you go to the kid's funeral and♥♥♥♥♥♥on his grave. And you♥♥♥♥♥♥on his parent's doormat. And then you wake up the next day and do it all over again, for the next 3 months with different kids. That's the kinda moral system we got in this game, that's the kind of characters you're meant to... somehow empathise with, or care about, because the gameplay is fine but pretty repetitive and the little bits of story and dialogue you get inbetween is CERTAINLY not well-written or engaging.
This is genuinely one of the worst stories for an idea that is SO good in theory. There's attention to detail spattered around the crime scenes you go to, and I really like that. But every time the story continues on, I physically can't stand it. If there was more focus on the crime scenes and their little stories and interactions, I think I would've enjoyed this game a lot more. But with how focused it is on its main story and characters, which are so unrelentingly awful... it's painful. Oh the mayor is telling you to fire black people again, then the next day says on the news that he doesn't know why the police force doesn't have black people. Oh he's complaining about gay people now. Oh, gotta hire some asian people to make some Japanese guy happy. Oh, someone's boyfriend just reported a♥♥♥♥♥♥on her... Turns out she's actually cheating on him. Oh, the main character is gonna see his wife and mend their relationship! A glimpse of hope! Nah, sorry he's been knocked out and in a coma. Now I get to speak to the press about what happened, oh I got 4 negative choices to make... hm, which one do I pick - it's quite difficult, I really don't know which way to be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a game full of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, I'm sure there's no way I can compete.
Welp, I think I enjoyed the absurdity of This is the Police more than I could ever enjoy its self-involved, morally devoid world for any longer. I love nihilistic and depressing stories but this is just plain awful storytelling and dialogue. Please don't homogenize your characters to this extent. In a world of unrelenting negativity, at least give a semblance of hope, even if it's false. I want to have a reason to play, other than "more bad things happen in bad world. Pretty bad, hey?"
3.5/10 I like the concept and art style. It's a technically well made game design wise but the story is honestly one of the worst I have encountered in any medium, be it film or video games or otherwise.

Although i ultimately recommend this game, there a few flaws you should be aware of.
First of all, well, is the game fun?
Yes. The game alternates a very simple, yet fun, management game where you are the chief of police. You will have to please / displease different characters in order to progress and sometimes you'll have to take moral choices, all while trying to solve a few investigations. In between the days, you will often see a few comic-like panels (with voiceover dialogue, similar to how max-payne did) that will narrate the story.
Is the story intriguing?
I ultimately liked it, but i will probably forget it in a few weeks. Nothing memorable, but will keep you interested enough to finish the game.
Is the game repetitive.
Yes. A lot. After the first few hours, i found myself bored at times and had to stop playing for a few days before i wanted to play again. The first few hours the game throws a lot of new stuff to you, so it stays fresh and engaging. Not so much for the second half of the game, where i just wanted the midnight to come so that i could finish the day.
Is it worth it?
I think so! There are a lot of gameplay hours for its price so if you like the trailer, buy it, it shows exactly what the game is made of. Remember that it will get extremly repetitive as you proceed. Thankfully you can quick-skip at least some comic panels that take forever to play out.

I'm not really that big of an MMO player or a hardcore TERA player, but I think I've played enough of the game to review. I have a level 65 Slayer and a level 65 Archer, and for the most part soloed through the story so far on them.
For a game that can run on laptops, TERA has pretty good graphics and a colorful, varied environment. Even if the action combat isn't that original has the grind aspect, the animations are fluid and put you into the battle. You'll be using 2-3 damaging combos and dodging attacks between them.You might be frustrated with the Archer class' inability to backflip oversmall walls or opponents and may even get cornered sometimes, so be wary of that. In addition I believe some classes (Lancer, Priest, Mystic?) are also meant to be support classes so don't plan on soloing with them.
Endgame content is for the most part just more grinding for top tier gears, but it's nothing too terrible -- for the most part it isn't too hard to find other players willing to grind with you. You pretty much want to at least max out T8 gear to fight in PvP with the other endgame players, which isn't that hard to do. There are definitely some cheap combos in PvP, and the big Corsair's Stronghold will probably lag if your PC isn't that great.
There are plenty of costumes available (at least for elins), accessories, and weapon skins, and if you wait for a sale you can buy a set for 2-3 characters with only $20. The calendar log in gifts are also pretty generous, although they mostly feature random rewards.
The storyline is pretty much the same for all characters, and most of the side quests don't drop good rewards or exp either. Vanguard quests should help you out if the story quests don't drop enough EXP. If you fight most BAMS before 65 you are also pretty much just doing it for the challenge, they don't drop anything too special. However as a whole TERA is still worth your while. And feel free to add me.

Tera is a 3D fantasy themed massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) developed by Bluehole Studio. The game was released in South Korea on January 25, 2011, in Japan on August 18, 2011, in North America on May 1, 2012, in Europe on May 3, 2012, and in Russia on February 26, 2015, with closed and open beta testings taking place before the launch dates. NHN Corporation, NHN Japan Corporation, En Masse Entertainment and Gameforge publishes the game in these regions, respectively. In February 2013 the game was renamed to Tera: Rising concurrently with the game's launch to the free-to-play model.
In September 2014 the game was renamed to "Tera: Fate of Arun" in the same patch that added a new level cap and expanded Tera's horizons with the new continent in Northern Arun: Val Oriyn "cut off from the rest of the world for centuries, Northern Arun is a land of savage jungles, colossal ruins, and the undiscovered homeland of the Barakas" The patch became effective on December 2014 in America and Europe .
