Home is a psychological thriller where every decision you make from what things you inspect through to where you choose to explore add up to give you one of multiple endings. "The protagonist" is trying to find his way home, but as you lead the way as "the narrator", our main man finds out just how much trouble they're in.
For a cheap game that lasts exactly an hour and a half as the developer claimed, it's amazingly effective. I played it after midnight in full darkness with headphones on as requested at the start of the game and it made it a very eerie playthrough. It'd be nowhere near as effective if I played it during the daytime, but I could probably have gotten away without the headphones given I've got a surround sound set up.
It's not the perfect game because one of the endings basically is a cop-out, but the other endings are much better. But again because this is a cheap game clearly made by a solo indie developer, I can forgive the minor flaws. It's a good thriller.
EDIT @ 2014-02-23:
More than a year since my original review date, I have not played this game again. Buy this game when it's cheap for a thrill, but I add the additional warning that the replay value of this game is very low.

Story 4.5: A bounty has been placed on an assassin's head and biker gangs are racing and killing each other for the bounty. That's it. I mean, it does explain why they're killing each other but it's pretty straightfoward. The game wasn't made for story which makes filling in for the story section kinda pointless. All I have to say is...yeah. Pretty straightfoward.
Visuals 5.5: Road Redemption looks OLD. I know the Unity Engine can showcase results far more superior than this game. It looks like a game from, like, 2008 at the most. The lighting can look pretty nice at times but the gameworld is filled with bland level layouts, muddy textures, unconvincing animations, and poor draw distances, even on max settings. Yet despite how old this looks, it's still demanding (again taking blame on the engine powering it).
Audio 7: The voice acting is exceptional at best but the music is forgetable.
Gameplay 6.5: Road Redemption borrows its inspiration from "Road Rash" and it works pretty well...for the first couple of hours. The concept here is pretty damn interesting. Combat on motorcycles! You use strikes, blocks, and weapons like pipes, swords, and guns and it can be both challenging and rewarding. It takes a bit of strategy to take your opponents down and win the race at the same time. Swords can decapitate enemies, but weak on helmets and driving and shooting can be hard which can take time to get used to. But due to the smooth controls, it's pretty easy to learn yet hard to master. But the combat gets very stale as you keep playing. Despite a few boss battles, campaign mode doesn't add much variety. Another problem is that it lacks content. It does have local and online multiplayer. But just like in single-player, it gets old fast. It also lacks polish. I've had a couple of times where I fell through the floor.
Verdict: Road Redemption has a pretty novel concept. But this concept grows stale as you keep playing. The lack of content and polish also keeps me from recommending this game.
Pros:
-Cool Concept
-Combat Can Be Fun...
Cons:
-...But It gets old quickly.
-Lack of Content and Polish

Where the ♥♥♥♥ is Batman..
This review will have minor spoilers throughout. You have been warned.
There are some very topical and ideologically sensitive ideas in this game. For example, Sexism, Racism, Prejudice, Homophobia, ♥♥♥♥, Murder, Religious intolerance, Religious extremism, Protests against numerous “socially justified” ideas. This is a game about corrupt police officers; You cannot possibly think that they would center the game around things such as children stealing gum balls from the candy shop.
This is the Police is a management sim on its face, an extremely narrative one. And before I get into it. I absolutely love what this game is going for but I have some serious criticisms about it. But I'll get to those later.
The setup is as such, you, the Chief of Police for the city of Freeburg named Jack Boyd is retiring in 180 days and desires to accumulate $500,000 in whatever way possible. Now, one of the main criticisms is that you cannot actually play as a good cop. You must at some level be corrupt. This is not really one of MY main critiques but I've heard many others complain about this. However, I believe it is inherent to have some amount of dealings with other, lets call them less than legal organizations for an authority to have any semblance of control over a large mass of people. Additionally, you are playing a character in a narratively driven game, not as yourself.
The main crux of this game is staring at a static 3D model of the scaled down city, and then responding and sending officers to calls. Each event is essentially a paragraph or two and you send an amount of officers and some support if desired such as SWAT and/or a paddy wagon. Which increase the success rate of your officers. It essentially operates with cooldowns and each call has a limited time to respond to; and its up to you to determine how many officers to send and whether or not a call even needs to be responded to.
Each call has different affects, sometimes the officers will call back to the station and ask what to do in certain situations or call for backup, in turn you decide to send more officers or not. These situations include multiple choice answers and selecting the right one will determine the success of your officers. More often than not, it relies on you having read and understood the situation at hand and dealing with it appropriately. For example, how to behave from the threat of violence as opposed to reacting to violence already committed all the way down to tricking a irate drug user or calmly walking up to someone deeply distraught.
There are a lot of systems in this game and they are all overlapping. I've heard complaints that they are heavily RNG-afied however they are very scripted and just have a high degree of learning to do to determine what is needed to not get your officers killed and still apprehend the offenders whilst being able to respond to the majority of calls.
There are detectives cases, and numerous affairs you must deal with. The game is split into 3 distinct chapters, you do not actually play all 180 days, otherwise the game would be 50 hours long. You'll deal with one major thing each chapter in addition to regular calls and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t from city hall trying to make your job much harder. For example: Serial killers, Mafia Wars, Political protests rampant with racial and sexist tensions all the while trying to appease the Mayor and City Hall as to not get your budget cut as well as deal with personal issues with your officers such as alcoholism.
There are gangs to take down, reading profiles and doing interrogations, hiring snitches and finding workarounds for less than legal activities. The calls are color coded:
yellow, orange, red for regular calls depending on time left to respond
purple for detective cases
green for social or community calls
grey/blue for something with affairs
black for important mass protests
My main issue is that the game is so narrativley driven that it feels a little contrived at points, it at times feels so chaotic with little means to correct course that it becomes overbearing. However, I feel its purposefully contrived in this manner to fulfill the narrative. I once thought a not Jack Boyd version of running the station would be fun but I've, after finishing, decided that that would ultimately be too much of an undertaking and take away from the overall feeling.
THE GIST
I could easily see myself re-playing this game because there are so many variables at play constantly and a couple of extremely major ones. But due to the highly narrative nature it would probably be far removed from the first playthrough. It's one of the more interesting titles I've played recently and one I found myself actually taking physical notes down for; I highly recommend the game but it's definitely not for everyone.

You are Hero (that's the default name anyway). One night, your father gets killed by a man in black with a red eye. You decide to get swole and take revenge. As you do this, you find yourself in a fighting tournament or two that seem to style themselves as "Boxing" but permit kicks, so maybe it's muay thai. I dunno. I'm a robot that lives in a server room playing video games. Along the way, you become Batman with allusions to the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (title image) and Silent Hill (I won't spoil this one but it's really dumb and I love it). You find love, you beat up a Russian. You get to participate in mecha fights! (Mecha fights make everything better... ) This game just has so many little jokes and references. It's amusing.
The game has stylized aesthetics and the music is this Eye of the Tiger remix that is actually pretty good. I made a boxing character because I totally read too much Hajime no Ippo. The game is sufficiently challenging. It took me over 300 (in-game) days to finish the game but I did waste a bunch of days on stuff that I'll mention later. The fights can get pretty tense as you sit there hoping RNGsus is in your favour but then complain when you repeatedly get knocked out because you have negative stamina. And then you win the fight anyway because your boxing character can do combos that deal over a third the opponent's health when they actually hit.
The storytelling is... sub-par. It's not anything to write home about. There's a main story and a series of substories. These substories do not seem to have much in the way of time limits. I locked myself out a substory by becoming a professional fighter so maybe I should've completed it but it's too late now. The main story has all of the usual tropes that you probably expect in a fighting game. And it has a very poorly written ending. It also kind of fades to black at an improper time.
Unfortunately the game does not seem to be balanced around being an all-around good fighter but rather by specializing in one stat. It tells you so much very early in the game. I would've liked for it to reward well-rounded players a little more. I did a hybrid of Power and Stamina, leaving out Agility. Agility determines how accurately you hit. So I have a heavy hitter than always misses. And even with my stamina training, I still found myself running out of stamina all the time. But maybe I'm just bad. Towards the end, the game becomes a bit of a grind and the pacing slows down drastically. Which leads up to the aforementioned poorly timed ending.
The game also does not explain some of the character interaction mechanics so I wound up wasting what must've been like 3 weeks trying to fix my friend's engine so he'd train with me. I actually had to look up what the deal was and apparently the engine never gets fixed, but that the lines that my friend says indicate whether or not I've 'chilled' with him long enough to get him to train with me. Also, let's be real here. I was the only one fixing his engine. The lazy SOB never got off the chair.
I do like the game, but I'm sitting on the fence with this one. I give it a pass because I found it amusing, but take this positive review with the grains of salt. It's probably a toss-up whether or not you find it to be a fun game. Let's not forget that the most important part of a game is whether or not it's fun.

A hidden gem. (And I'm not a massive fan of survival games in general).
HLTB?  About 8-9hrs.
Hour 0-1. Dead again. Repeat. Dead again. Repeat. Urrr. this is a bit annoying. Almost gave up.
Hours 1-2. Didn't freeze to death, but ants, snakes, wolves and that damn hog... causing me issues.
Hours 2-5. Still many close calls, but scraping through ok. Getting some decent gear.
Hours 5-8. Feeling like a boss. Death is rare, and if it happens I'm at fault.
Hour 8+. Made it. Despite a slightly dull climax, I feel a deep sense of satisfaction.
So here's the deal (which I hope will fairly explain away some of the negative reviews); it's very easy to die when you start playing, there are many arghhh moments where you curse the randomness of death, and I admit I was close to abandoning the game but it had a charm (nice design, atmosphere, even good music) which kept me playing ...and at some point it all just clicked into place - you learn what you need to survive, where to get it, and figure out ways to avoid hazards and close scrapes.
Often death is not as unfair as it seems - I died a few times from dehydration or drinking contaminated water, and cursed the lack of water and filters but later in the game I realised  I could
. Argh. So simple. This is part of the satisfaction, you feel yourself getting better (although never to a point where you don't respect your surroundings).
As for the negative reviews, I understand why some people would get annoyed at first, (even bored) but having beaten the game I can happily say anyone who is grinding (or being beaten by randomness) ...well, you're doing it wrong! ;)

So to start with the game is fun, and if you like the FNAF games so far then you will enjoy this entry. First the good, the scares are back and so is the tension. Every time you go for the door, there is this excruciating moment of doubt that happens right before you go for your light, you think damn did I hear anything...... (click). This moment never stops and you will have a hard time acclimating to it. The design of the animatronics are  well done and very menacing, they have dropped the uncanny valley cute but off vibe for a straight nightmare inducing horror one. Now for the downside, the amount of content in this game is light both in gameplay and story. Gone are all the cameras and rooms packed to the brim with set dressing, and filling the game with a sense of scale and providing ambiance. I miss the little posters on the wall that seemed to change and move, the slight variations on how the animatronics may appear on the cams in the rooms and the little thing you may catch out of the corner of your eye that may catch you off guard and mess with your game plan. (the phantoms from 3 where great at this).
[Spoilers Ahead] The story isn’t bad as much as it doesn't add much to the overall lore, it is a lead up to the infamous bite of ‘87. The game is played out over 5 nights (duh) leading up to a birthday that will be held at Freddy Fazbears. Each day the player/child is tormented by who I assume is his older sibling and his/her friends each day. You can't help but feel bad for this kid who you can tell has issues as he talks to a stuffed Fredbear toy and has the whole gang in plush form yet paradoxically  is also terrified of the actual animatronics. You see the child at home or at Freddy's playing and trying to get away from the various mascots, while being tortured by his sibling their friends. This all ends with the sibling and his/her friends bullying the protagonist and causing the bite. Thats it, thats your lot, no insight into the purple guy, the puppet, the ghost of the murdered kids no indication that the the mascots have been possessed yet. All we get are a cameo of the purple man and possibly shadow Bonnie and shadow Freddy. Lets hope that the October update can give us a bit more lore wise and some new scares.

Don't get me wrong, Five Nights at Freddy's 4 is quite the interesting game, it serves a pretty haunting and deep storyline, along with an interesting concept of a game. However, this game certainly is not THAT good, I don't think it's very deserving of the "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews out there.
So, you play as the victim from the infamous bite of 87, which is quite a nice twist in the storyline. Haunted over the event, the child begins to fear these animatronics, and pictures them as these freakish monster creatures. I wont dive to in depth with the story, this is for you to figure out yourself.
I think Five Nights at Freddy's 4 is a great achievement as well, considering it was made in Clickteam Fusion, however the engine the game uses is actually a major flaw... You see, I personally think gameplay over graphics, however, considering this game's visuals aren't all too stunning, the animation quality can sometimes seem un-natural, and the game's only control is to click on doors and hold down a few keys every now shows that this game lacks both gameplay and graphics. People are going to begin to say "DO YOU NOT KNOW WHAT IT MEANS FOR A GAME TO BE POINT AND CLICK!?" which I do know, I just don't think it really works out. You see, when you're trying to make a horror game that's meant to be immersive and meant to be creepy, you'd think you would get a little more out of it.
Another thing I didn't really like is that the game... isn't scary... Yeah, you probably think I'm just trying to make myself look brave and all, but I'm not. Even when PewDiePie played the game, he never flinched. That guy overreacts to everything, and the fact that he doesn't to this game probably says something. Sure, you may find it scary, but personally, I don't, and I know a hand full of people who agree with me.
Pros:
- Interesting concept
- Intriguing story-line
- A nice twist to the series
Cons:
- Lacks gameplay
- Lacks immersive visuals
- Relies too heavily on jump-scares to be scary
- Animation quality is pretty bad
- Serves very little hours of gameplay (if this is what you call gameplay)
If you are expecting a rating out of me, I would personally say it's a 5/10, I understand other people may actually enjoy this game, and that's great for you if you do, however I didn't find much out of it. Also, a 5 isn't THAT bad. It's a mediocre game, that's all.
Also, just throwing this out, this doesn't change my perspective on the game, but I think it's something that should be made clear. This game's fanbase if awful, possibly one of the worse fandoms out there. It's filled with false hype, over-saturation, and childish behavior. In fact, I bet I will get a comment telling me how wrong I am, by someone who can't prove even prove me wrong.
Lastly, this isn't self advertisement, in fact I find this to be shameful on myself. I noticed this review is getting more and more traffic very fast and therefor it's bound for someone to recognize me. Yes, I am that guy who made the "How to animate FNAF in SFM tutorial" along with a handful of other FNAF videos. I regret it at moments, and don't animate anything Five Nights at Freddy's unless it's like super requested that I do one video in particular. A FNAF video that started off as a joke quickly escalated into more request overtime. I don't mind making them, just as long as I can take a short break and make a "whatever video" or something, which I do. Call me a hypocrite, however, I never once said I liked FNAF in the past."

I got this in a bundle and wasn't expecting a ton from it, but it turned out to be pretty good. What would otherwise be a fairly standard old school adventure/horror game (which at times telegraphs a bit obviously what's going to happen next) is saved by subverting a couple adventure game conventions. For one, instead of requiring you to collect every item and examine every pixel and "do ALL the things!" to progress, it gives you the option to deliberately NOT do/get things, which changes the dialog/story. It also has a mechanic for not only making plot decisions but allowing you to interpret the story in-game. It's flawed, but it's not a bad way to spend an hour.

Let me start by saying this game at its core, is a pretty good game. I enjoyed the gameplay, visuals and characters so far. My main gripe, like many others is Ubisoft's decision to implement a layer of VMProtect which essentially turns your PC into an emulator.
I've tolerated Denuvo because despite its flaws, it always valued keeping a very low performance cost when implemented correctly, RIME is the only example I can think of that was a poor implementation that hurt performance due to have way to many triggers.
VMProtect on the other hand, is pretty much confirmed to lower performance as your essentially running a virtual machine on top of the games code and Denuvo. We know from what Denuvo has stated, that it only does its "checks" during non critical periods, such as the startup screen or a loading screen. From what has been shown in AC: Origins, VMProtect is constantly running in the game's core at all times.
I've refunded this game, which is a shame. Ubisoft's agenda in anti piracy measures once again causes them to make all the wrong decisions and hurt legit, paying customers. Although, coming from a CEO who says 95% of PC users are pirates, it doesn't surprise me they would prioritize these types of decisions.

This game may look "too simple", with very basic graphic, but it have a lot of interesting aspect:
- Interesting Gameplay, with a great difficulty, not too easy and not very hard (standard difficulty)!
- Different Heroes, Squads, Categories, Spells...
- Lot of Upgrades, Skills, Improvements you can do
- Many Ways to Play / win the battles, you can make strategies, go with only Archers, Full of Magic with Wizzards or with Badass Heroes & Infantry OR ALL TOGHETER!
- Lot of Monsters, Challenges.
- Many Hours of Gameplay.
There are few bad things you may dislike:
- Lot of Griding to improve your stuff, you have to replay "easy levels" again & again to earn money to make your squad powerful, to keep going.. it may be annoying at some point
- The Other 2 difficulties are just insane & useless for loot sometimes since you can get the same amount of gold in the next 2 missions with less time in standard difficulty.. also cannot be done even if you max out most of your characters.. it's only for confirmed player & tryharders..
- There is no tutorial at the begining to explain how to improve things, how to play "correctly". also information about characters, heroes is not visible, sometimes you want to check what the specifics of this or that, you end up buying it.. need a clear interface, with all info & improvements about it...
- No Story mission (or not clear), but it's not that important, all you have to do is kill the bad guys!
Beside these points, this game is great, a little gem, something you can play repeatedly, you can sometimes do 2-3 parties in 10min for fun, or spend more hours griding & improving, playing the story missions..
RECOMMENDED

I am torn on this game. The mechanics are great, the story is well written and makes sense regardless on how you end up playing the game (corrupt or not), and while you end up with a heap of stuff going on it's introduced at a rate that makes it easy to keep track of everything. All the different gameplay types blend together seamlessly.
That being said, there are some parts of the game that are more painful than anything else. There are a couple of levels in which your entire force are incredibly tired and/or don't show up to work, leaving you being quite understaffed on the day and it's more frustrating than anything else because there isn't actually anything you can do to stop that situation occurring. But this frustration is part of the immersive nature of the game as I was getting quite invested in my police force. That being said, to win the game you have to solve a puzzle that, as far as I can tell, comes entirely down to luck and it won't tell you how close you are to solving the puzzle, it'll just either give you the ending of the game or it won't. Which is also a massive let down.
There are some elements of the game that are too luck-based for my liking (avoiding spoilers), though you kinda do need an element of luck, but overall I did enjoy playing through the game (even if I didn't come close to having the money at the end), just be prepared for a terrible ending.

Basically you're the Freeburg Police Chief who is nearing retirment in 180 days, but doesn't have enought to live the life he wants after leaving the job. You solve this early on by either choosing to be bought out by the mafia or staying a straight cop. From there on you control the police depatment's daily operations. You will have to make decisions such as how many officers to send on every 911 call, and piece together your detictives final investigations through a fairly straightforward puzzle. Sounds fun at first, but get VERY repetitive after only playing for a short amount of time. Your decisions also don't seem to affect the final outcome from most emergency calls. Usually it doesn't matter if you send two cruddy officers, or three outstanding ones. Either way somehow the suspect will get away and a civillian will be killed after responding to something crazy like a clown being to loud blowing balloons in the park.
I'd recommend only getting this game if it's on sale! I think it's a good match for anyone looking to play something simple for maybe a half hour at a time.

Like many I was excited by the game's concept, but disappointed by the delivery.  Choice is an illusion, and the game is unforgiving for beginners.  And by "unforgiving for beginners" I mean you have to either 1) get lucky or 2) die multiple times before you learn the mechanics.  This game is painful, and I say this loving painful resource mgmt strategy games (I have literally 100s of XCOM hours).
On my 3rd start I thought I was finally getting the hang of the system, the mission types, and consequences of my choices.  At the first major decision point I decided not to use force
.  I later sent 3 well trained officers against a guy with a knife and two died.  I sent out 4 more with the swat team to a bank robbery and two more fell (4 dead in a single shift).  Without the support of city hall it was over pretty quickly.  Start #4 I chose to use force
My snitch found the two officers who would testify against me with two days left.  They were on the next day's shift so I held off buying the mob's target officers event until they were available to target.  The next day I bought the mob target... "you're target job will be tomorrow at 10:00"... ok... would have been nice to know before, but... no problem... I'll just switch their shift.  That day the two officers didn't show up for work.  I lost 90% of my salary and 50% staff (staff cuts chosen at random not by you).  Needless to say I found myself at the end of play through #4 quickly after that.
Could I have gone back, replayed every decision I made, and used the mob hit as the dev intended once I learned you had to account for a day's lag? Yes.  But after getting hit with crippling dice rolls/non intuitive mechanics for the 5th time I was done.  I've read others reviews comparing the game to Paper's Please, but it's more like Life Goes On.  You restart the game multiple times learning/memorizing the level, performing the same actions, until you start to feel like that's the point of the game.
would not recommend

You mourn the loss of a good subordinate, yet don't care so much when a drunk lazy police officer gets himself into a car accident. You feel bad when you have to cooperate with bad guys, but console yourself with the idea of exterminating it one day.
There's a fairly wide variety of events to prevent them being repetitive.
Wonderful voice acting, sleek graphics, beautiful music, intriguing story, well thought-out gameplay and a damn good game!
Looking forward to support such games and developers further.

Hmm.. if you ask me what I think about this MMO, I'd say give it a GO! Yes, it's old. The 2nd MMO after Aion Online and you guys would prefer Blade & Soul but that game is more Graphics and PVP. Tera however has a huge chunk of PVE and PVP goodness. If you're the type who enjoys insane dungeons from 5 Man - 30 Man Raids with Normal or Hard Modes, TERA is your Go-To. It's no puny point and click, this game really requires skill. Real time if I must say? GG if your ping is above 300. Fair warning.
Now, graphics wise, this used to be the bomb until newer MMO's came out but Tera holds its place with constant updates from dungeons to fashion and new classes. This game has its own twist to the PVP thirsty people. 3 vs 3 to 20 vs 20. You fight to protect/defend your castle, shoot down Ships, Roll people over with Cannons and break down doors to thrash your enemies crystals and win the game! Oh , good Crystals and Gear help a LOT in certain PVP runs like Fraywind Canyon.. so Gear up! Winners steal a load of points and earn great rewards to obtain mats to craft their End Game gear.
With Aion Online being nearly outdated, Tera Online recently introduced what I'd say a "mini-merge" of Aion's plus points into the game with FLYING MOUNTS. Though only in selected maps, you get to fly on a Pegasus or a.. well, a winged lion lol! What more could you ask for? I personally wish Tera would introduce a NEW RACE and perhaps open UNDERWATER quests and dungeons, Undine Race perhaps? I sniff a Spear Class! Hng!
Besides new job classes, (though lazy Blue Hole Studios and their gender locked♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tera is always surprising us with new content to keep its players. Guilds and Alliance systems are also pretty unique, working together to pump up the score board to earn yourselves a Sky Castle (with whales flying...?).. yes a Flying Castle for the Top 10 Guilds of each season within a 1 month duration!
Optimization wise however has a little bit of a turn off. Though understandable as Tera did come out in 2011 so do forgive it. At the very lease, it's fresh to the eyes for those WoW players to see an 'Asian' version of their MMO with much better graphics. You may need to tweak certain things on Tera as it has pretty unstable optimization but it's definitely bearable and workable with edits. There are many guides out there so fret not~ (^・ω・^ )
So.. why not try?
I'm on Celestial Hills PVE RP Server. (I don't really RP, but I enjoy the people here. Creative people and cheerful) but anyhow, enjoy if you do decide to give it a shot~ ♥
Hope to see you on the other side!

This is a solid stealth game.
The ball weapon is surprisingly versatile. You can toss it around the corner by throwing it at a wall. You can also use it to distract enemies. And, after you charge it up, you can destroy enemies with it. If you throw it correctly, the ball will bounce off the enemy and back to your hands. Otherwise, it will bounce elsewhere, and you will have to chase it....
Unless you use a power-up.  There are four power-ups that you can use, and by grabbing coins and beating levels, you can purchase stronger power-ups or more uses of power-ups. One of them returns the ball to you if it gets away from you. Another gives you a temporary cloak, which is perhaps too powerful. I recommend not using the cloak power-up except on those levels where beating it under par time is way too difficult or impossible without it.
The only real problem is that the mouse cursor doesn't change shape and color in-game. My cursor is a small white arrow, and it makes it difficult to aim quickly in a bright and colorful game like this unless you're constantly looking at it.
Nevertheless, I recommend this game.

Rewriting this because I think some things need cleared up a bit for people not familiar with this sort of story...Key's storys have a tendency to give you excruciating detail into characters and backgrounds.(more below)
Nothing negative to say about this game for my own part. It was one of the rare gems I've seen in recent years and is a strong pull of Quality over Quantity (as per hours of play). I never would have heard about this had it not been for the Steam sale, but it would be well worth even the full price at $9.99 (if you can justify going to a movie theatre, this game is worth at least as much).
Important things to note:
~This "game" is basically a short book. No choices, to make beside whether to click ahead or listen through a scene.
~There is a lot of detailed description. Some people might find it to be too much, but given that the entirety of the story takes place in less than a week's time for the character, it is necessary. By the end of it you should have a good grasp on the world, the main characters as well as the world's history that brought it to the present state. If you find yourself in any way clueless it's probably an error on your own ability to read and understand.
~The story is emotionally driven primarilly.
If you're action oritented, look elsewhere.
If you need something that aims to grip you quickly, look elsewhere.
~Full appreciation will come from not having a standard set in your mind for things to be like in real life as it is now. Consider the world that the story is in.

But somehow after that, this part is quite boring and dull. The outside part was more interesting part for me personally and I quite enjoyed it throughout until the ending. (although the ending was 'hanging'). After finishing the game, I looked up the audio CDs that were put up in youtube though so I already watched the full ending, which I recommend you to do it also.
So for the conclusion, I do recommend this game for you people who enjoyed 'science fiction' type stories albeit it has some flaws. The game is still very enjoyable and the 'missing part' of the games can be searched using google. My rating : 7/10

I saw this as I was browsing through the depths of Steam's store and picked it up on a whim. Right after I purchased it, I began reading through this visual novel which was made by 'Key', the same studio behind many great visual novels and anime including 'Clannad' and 'Angel Beats!'. The first half or so seems to be dragged out quite a bit with banter between the narrator and a robot named Yumemi Hoshino. I became mainly enthralled with the concept of the setting, a post-apocalytpic world that has been occupied by war machines. The game features excellent artwork and music composition. The ending, much like in Key fashion, ripped my heart out and tore my soul asunder. If you are a fan of kinetic visual novels, or even slightly interested in visual novels as is, I extremely recommend that you purchase it. It'll only last you a few hours, but the experience will hopefully last with you for a good long while like it has with myself.

Right, so let me say a couple of things before I actually get to my review. First off, I got this game via a Humble Bundle, and did not pay full price. Second, and frankly more important, I did not finish the game. Now, Punch Club is a fighter management game in which you control a fighter as he goes through a fighting career to avenge his father or something. You customize him throughout his career by selecting his fighting style through a fairly standard skill tree system. The actual fights are little more than cutscenes where you can switch things up in between rounds if things are going too great. Now, clearly I don't think this game is worth the time, but let's look at the good and bad anyway.
The Good
- Beatiful 16-bit graphics. The game is just pleasant to look at, and makes great use of its art style.
- Unique fighting paths that genuinely change how your fighting is going to go.
- There is plenty of fun side stuff to do, and most of it is fairly entertaining.
- There are hundreds of references scattered throughout the game, from Pulp Fiction to TMNT, and there are plenty of things for just about anyone to get a light chuckle out of.
- Like many management games, this one is good at keeping you hooked in... at first.
- A very fun game... at first.
The Bad
- The stat decay system. Holy crap. At first, not training and having your stats lower slowly sounds like a solid way to add some challenge into the game, but as soon as you raise any stat past 13, say goodbye to improvement. Later in the game it is absolutely mental how quickly your high stats decay, and it's insane how much time you have to put into training to maintain a solid statline. Normally I like to keep these points brief, but I cannot stress enough how much this system sucks. It is the key reason that I have to give this game a down, because after you leave the early-mid game, it becomes a complete drag, and this system is the entire reason for it. It's a fair idea taken way too far, and completely screws you over in the late game. It takes actually maybe 20 minutes to train up between each fight. The fights are like, a minute and a half long. It's such a hassle, that I think it will be a turn-off for anyone not heavily invested into management games. This game was really fun, until this damn system tanked it. I'm not even mad, shut up.
- Bland characters. That's it.
Overview
Frankly, I'm pretty torn on this because there's so much good here, and it's ruined by one large bad thing. Punch Club is a fun game. It's quirky, it's substantial, it can be somewhat varied, and the story is somewhat decent. It's also beautiful for an 16-bit game, and has all the tools necessary to be an incredible deal for ten bucks. However, after buying these tools, it went back to the store and brought 50,000 angry wasps, and then threw them into your eyes. I'm not even mad. I'M FINE! THE DECAY SYSTEM IS FINE! I'M NOT EVEN MAD! ♥♥♥♥ YOU!
Tl;dr: So close, but the decay system is such a kick in the sack, that it's not worth the money. Worth a buy if you're really into management games.

This game is an interesting experiment, one that doesn't always work, and can lead to frustration at times, but I still love the concept enough to keep playing. If you're looking for a new kind of survival game outside of the typical Minecraft-esque slog, this game may be for you.
If I had to describe the game, I'd say it's a mix of Don't Starve and Rogue Legacy, two games which I love. Essentially, you are put into a top-down wilderness, where you must gather resources to craft items and food, and stay in shelters to avoid the elements. Standard survival game stuff. However, the world is divided into specific types of areas, where only specific types of items can be obtained. These small pieces of the game world are interconnected by a river, which you can ride via makeshift raft. You can't make the raft go upstream though (believe me, I've tried), forcing you to choose which specific locations you must travel to, so that you can obtain whatever specific supplies you need. It's a brilliant idea in my opinion.
The art style is kind of nice, although it looks somewhat cheaper than other games with similar art styles (Firewatch and the like). One of my biggest complaints with the look is a lack of a health meter, which makes it incredibly confusing to figure out how close you are to dying. The music is occasionally annoying, but almost always a pleasant distraction from the game's dificult nature.
Speaking of difficulty, the game's biggest problem, one that's forced me from being able to reccommend it is a huge dificulty spike. You start the game with nearly no advercaries, besides the river possibly. However, the very next thing it introduces are wild boars, which are able to break bones in one hit. It's astounding how little thought was put into this. Also, as far as I've been able to figure out, you can't craft legitimate weapons. making the only option for not getting killed by a wild animal being to stay by a campsite, or to flee to a new area. And then they add wolves on top of the boars, which can travel in packs, making an encounter with one essentially a death sentence.
I wish I could reccommend this game, because I love the concept, and a lot of the stylistic presentation is excellent. But this is one of the worst difficulty spikes I've seen in a game ever. Get it on a sale, or in a Humble Bundle (that's how I got it) if you're interested. I'll update the review if they address these problems, but for now, my thumbs down stands.

I have been following this game since it's been on Itch.io and have been patiently waiting for this moment. At last Streets of Rogue has come to Steam! This is a great rogue-lite title (as the name suggests) with a great soundtrack and amazing gameplay. The amount of detail put in to this game is truly outstanding; comedic dialogue, moddable weapons, variety of pickups and perks, funny item descriptions, and crazy over-the-top gameplay complete with punching people through walls, shrinking and growing people, and bloody gibblets of meat! with that said this is a very early version with very few levels and a fraction of the content, Unless you want to support the developers (like me) or are absolutely certain you'll love this game, I'd wait a while for more content to be added.

-----------------FUN
This game is very entertaining, and bigger than its file size suggests (another virtue of the game).
The experience changes every time, and you can change it even more.
Randomly generated maps, with many dynamic NPC types.
- The base game has 11 stages right now, each of which is can change every time without
losing its essence.
Lots to do, many ways to do it.
- Whether you're killing a guy in his apartment or freeing a gorilla from a secret lab, there's
usually an air duct you can poision, hatred you can create, something to hack, people to send
in, sneaky items or a big bomb to use.
Many different interactions and details.
- You can buy, steal, fight , get mugged by, and talk to many of the characters in this game.
Mutators and items to change the gaming experience.
- Such as giving everyone a rocket launcher or setting a level timer.
There are lots of items.
- drugs
- guns
- meelee
- armor
- explosives
- many more miscellaneous items, like a trap that paralyzes people or a remote that blow up
any slaves of yours.
There are many characters.
- Around 25 classes, each with it's own playstyle.
- Characters that you can create.
- play alone / w friends
-----------------REPLAYABLE
People always want to know: "How long before I get bored?" With Streets of Rogue, the answer is probably at least a 2-digit long amount of hours.
Even if you're somebody who can get bored of an expansive game like this in ten hours, you're paying $15 for ten hours of fun in a place where you can control your experience to the smallest detail is an amazing deal in the real world.
For everyone else, the likely answer is that you'll play the game for forty hours before beginning to get slightyl bored and discover mutators, hunting for achievements, and changing your playstyle for a new perspectiv and hours more of fun. See You have died of Dysentery's guide about this.
You won't get bored of this game very soon.
There are many people with over 50 hours right now, and some with over 100. Here are some examples:
★ Ansam (177 hrs)
★ ABS_Page (122 hrs)
★ Viiper (115 hrs)
★ braboobsierre (109 hrs)
★ Heckin' Jews (80 hrs)
★ Fatterie~ (54 hrs)
and many more...
Overall, it takes a long time to see and do everything, and since the game is multiplayer, you get yet another new experience with every lobby you join.
-----------------VERSATILITY
While this game may appeal only to a certain group of people on steam, Streets of Rogue covers a pretty good scope of game types and tastes.
You can play the game several ways:
- A tactical shooter (Just shoot from behind cover and advance everywhere like an army guy or whatever, you know?)
- Bullet Hell Rogue-Like
- (Weird) Society Simulator (There's a lot to observe in this game, so observe it all)
- Stealth Game
The game's graphics might not appeal to everyone, but the shadows, lights, animation, and detailed pixel art are worth a shot. I'm generally a First-Person only player, but SoR has been an exception for me.
-----------------COMMUNITY
Many developers promise a lot, and fade away after a few months. The developer of this game updates every two weeks, and has done so for many months, steadily adding more and more to the game. There's only one dev, but updates are generally great.
This game also has a (mostly) responsive and friendly community. That is to say, we all share ideas, and discuss the game's future.

This game took me by surprise, to be honest. I was expecting an unbalanced death trap with broken mechanics and simplistic graphics. Instead, I got a beautifully made game with multiple playstyles to choose from and a reward system that, unlike other rogue-likes, makes dying less frustrating. As well, I can begin to see how much potential it holds, especially with its customization. To put it simply, Streets of Rogue is a diamond in the rough that all gamers can enjoy.
Pros:
+ A wide range of characters/playstyles to choose from.
+ Gameplay is adaptable and allows for creativity.
+ Never a dull moment, especially when Disasters kick in.
+ In-game factions that are balanced in their benefit-to-consequence ratios.
+ The art style, though simplistic, has its charms and is very atmospheric.
+ The music is extremely fitting and it pumps me up beyond belief.
+ Multiplayer and Co-op for those who enjoy teamkilling and slaughtering your friends.
+ Make your game harder/easier by implementing 'hacks' such as everyone despising you or Creative Mode.
+ I was too lazy to break into a house so I blew it up with the equivalent of a nuke, killing at least 15 people and a gorilla.
As for the cons, please take into account that they are not meant to criticize and more to point out what Early Access (as of me writing this on 3/11/2017) has to offer at the moment.
Cons:
- Missions can get a little repetitive.
- Only two zones to play through (though this can be 'solved' by turning on Endless Mode).
Where it stands now, Streets of Rogue is an exhilirating experience but I can imagine how much fun it will be to play Co-op once I get my pals to play with me. It can be a little monotonous after a few hours but that is remedied by striving to unlock everything the game currently has to offer. I would give this enjoyable experience a 7.9/10.

The original intention of this game was to take Road Rash to the next level.
The next level must mean unbalanced gameplay, unoriginal levels, frustrating controls and a lack of direction.
I kickstarted this game back in 2013 and it was definitely not worth the wait. I regretted backing this game once I got an email survey asking my opinion on adding guns to the game. Guns completely ruin the concept of being a Road Rash game by giving an incredible advantage to anyone behind you. Combine that with incredibly accuracy when using a mouse and there is nothing stopping you once you get a gun. The "boss" fights in this game are totally trivial as long as you have some bullets left.
In 2014 I got the alpha key for this game and it was laughable. It was exactly as bad as all the updates on the kickstarter had lead to me believe. I figured my kickstarter money (as usual) was wasted. I never expected this game to actually finish to completion, so many years later! It is better than the alpha but can not live up to its dream of Road Rash.
Most of the levels are winding roads which don't offer much challenge unless a car blindsinds you over a hill or you forget to hold the "turn sharp" button. There is a level where you jump around on rooftoops with a rocket pack on your motorcycle and thankfully it only shows up twice. Other than guns being in the game this is the single worst feature of the entire game.
The racing, if you can even call it that, in this game is all about managing your nitro, if you run out of nitro and there are no enemies around you have pretty much lost. The nitro lets you boost at such high speeds for such a long time and it is so easy to replenish. It seems to completely negate the acceleration stat of the motorcycle you are using and makes everything feel the same.
Despite being a roguelike where traditionally every game starts off at the same random point, you unlock persistent upgrades through your various attempts which seems like a way of brute forcing your way through victory rather than relying on gaining skill as a racer.
Road Roash wasn't a roguelike with rubberbanding AI and a strong focus on combat. It was a racing game where you could race dirty. Road Rash also had a clean sense of progression, with saving money you earned through the races to buy new bikes to go faster. Now the only thing you can buy are some random upgrades which could make or break your game if the store doesn't want to be your friend on the current run.

When we put this to the test with four friends last night, we got bored because of the randomness - it is surprisingly easy to act like a computer-driven character.
+There are different modes of gameplay that are fairly distinct
+Controller support is good, and there are great ways to 'swap' roles each round
+Its cheap
-The game modes and core design need to be worked out more, some way to make it more competitive
-Graphics look stock from some game-building program - there is no unifying theme (i.e. skeletons, ninjas, snowmen, and then hand-drawn images etc.)
-Local co-op only, although this would not be fun online

First of all, i'm going to give y'all the pros:
To be honest - Watch Dogs 2 is Packing a vibrant, immersive open world, likeable cast of characters, and an engaging plot, it is (VERY) good-looking, entertaining hacking that's not afraid to make a statement on today's technology-obsessed society. Silenced guns. Silent guns aren't silent. Using that silenced pistol with the scope has the same effect as firing off a naval cannon to enemies. This game is an interesting experiment, one that doesn't always work, and can lead to frustration at times, but I still love the concept enough to keep playing. If you're looking for a new kind of survival game outside of the typical Minecraft-esque slog, this game may be for you.
If I had to describe the game, I'd say it's a mix of Don't Starve and Rogue Legacy, two games which I love. Essentially, you are put into a top-down wilderness, where you must gather resources to craft items and food, and stay in shelters to avoid the elements. Standard survival game stuff. However, the world is divided into specific types of areas, where only specific types of items can be obtained. These small pieces of the game world are interconnected by a river, which you can ride via makeshift raft. You can't make the raft go upstream though (believe me, I've tried), forcing you to choose which specific locations you must travel to, so that you can obtain whatever specific supplies you need. It's a brilliant idea in my opinion.
The art style is kind of nice, although it looks somewhat cheaper than other games with similar art styles (Firewatch and the like). One of my biggest complaints with the look is a lack of a health meter, which makes it incredibly confusing to figure out how close you are to dying. The music is occasionally annoying, but almost always a pleasant distraction from the game's dificult nature.
Speaking of difficulty, the game's biggest problem, one that's forced me from being able to reccommend it is a huge dificulty spike. You start the game with nearly no advercaries, besides the river possibly. However, the very next thing it introduces are wild boars, which are able to break bones in one hit. It's astounding how little thought was put into this. Also, as far as I've been able to figure out, you can't craft legitimate weapons. making the only option for not getting killed by a wild animal being to stay by a campsite, or to flee to a new area. And then they add wolves on top of the boars, which can travel in packs, making an encounter with one essentially a death sentence.
I wish I could reccommend this game, because I love the concept, and a lot of the stylistic presentation is excellent. But this is one of the worst difficulty spikes I've seen in a game ever. Get it on a sale, or in a Humble Bundle (that's how I got it) if you're interested. I'll update the review if they address these problems, but for now, my thumbs down stands.

'The Flame in the Flood' is a game that I want to enjoy more than I currently do, because after beating the campaign once, I don't want to go back.
First impressions matter, and I had a horrible beginner experience. I was forced to alt-tab within a minute to even learn the game's primary objective, and this might be the first time I've ever encountered such a lack of information. All the game had to say was "take your raft down-river and don't die", but it left me so direction-less that I almost put it down. The new-player experience is poor, and the few on-screen instructions are given without much context. One of the first things the game told me was how to 'shoo' crows, without telling me why. Is this useful information? Are the crows a threat? Well the reason was written on a billboard that I missed, and in hindsight, I would have preferred the game to tell me about the existence of a sprint key, because the first bear I ran into had an easy lunch.
I am not a particularly fast thinker, and as a new player, I needed more time to understand the various menus and crafting priorities. Inventory management is a big part of this game, and crucial decisions have to be made about throwing things away, merging stacks of items, or where they go. However, because opening the inventory does not pause the game, everything is done on a timer. I starve for every second in the menus, and that relentless pressure is not only tiring, but infuriating. I want to have fun exploring and surfing down the rapids, and when I forgot about the constant hunger or hydration, I was. But the constant scramble for resources, especially against the excessive stat drain on endless mode, made the entire game a time-trial chore.
Repeating music and area layouts are noticeable, but I was more concerned with the frequency of failed starts. In one of my latest attempts the first four camp sites had wolves, and with no means to bypass them I died of tiredness. My experience with 'The Flame in the Flood' could be partially explained by a growing dislike in craft & survive games, (or roguelites), but I hope this is the last time those mechanics stop me playing a video-game that I would like to continue.

For those owning a Samsung Smart TV and having their FPS locked at 24 (or anything lower than 60) like I did, please follow this simple suggestion that worked perfectly for me:
Go to Nvidia control panel, in the display category click on "Adjust desktop size and position". Select a scaling mode, choose Full-Screen (mine was set to aspect ratio that's why the screen locked its refresh rate to 24 when I opened The Flame in the Flood), press apply and there you have it.

There's a lot of attention to detail in this game. For example, in the tutorial, you could break down the door with your FISTS instead of opening it normally and the tutorial guy reacts with a "WOAHHH THAT WAS AWESOME I'VE NEVER SEEN ANYONE OPEN A DOOR LIKE THAT" (or equivalent). If you bust down the shopkeeper's door, she scolds you. If you kill her, the tutorial guy has a line of dialogue for that. If you kill a guy the tutorial guy wanted you to tranquilize, there's a different line of dialogue there too. If you walk into the ladies' bathroom, your boss reprimands you for it later on. It's really interesting seeing all the different reactions the characters have.
The dozens of classes allow for many, many different possible playstyles, and I've still yet to fully explore them all. So far, I've only really "played" one class- the doctor. That speaks to how much replayability is in this thing.
It's a really great game, and I definitely recommend it if you liked roguelikes like Wayward Souls or Pixel Heroes: Byte & Magic. Heck, even if you didn't like roguelikes I'd still recommend it, just for its humor.

Funny because I was randomly thing of Road Rash before I knew this game existed.  Then I saw this, and I thought, "Yeah just wait for the price to come down."
But then I was like WAIT A MINUTE, vehicle racing destruction is probably MY FAVORITE genre of all time.  Why?  a) I like vehicle stuff.  I like driving sunderers in Planetside 2. Remembering Road Rash got me to thinking about Twisted Metal and then the follow-up games when the devs split.  A whole genre kind of died.
BRING IT BACK.  To review the game, it's a grind but in a way that the grind means playing Road Rash until you get the XP to level up.  I'm cool with that. I see the love put into this, and it brought back a love for a genre I forgot how much I loved.  I overwhelmingly support buying this now and not waiting because the people behind this are sincere in what they're doing and developing.  They're also doing it to a very high standard. TL:DR:
Game itself is fantastic, but can't reccomend because of Ubisofts choice to use both Denuvo + VMProtect which is crippling performance, as well as the persistant and annoying audio issues.
Actual Review:
Ok so firstly, I LOVE this game, the actual game itself is brilliant and I dont think they could have improved it much more.
They've kept the stuff that worked from the previous games, threw out what didnt work and introduced a lot of new mechanics that allow for a much greater dimension of freedom and choosing how you play.
The game is a little more RPG'ish now, similiar to the witcher with the gear and combat systems, though in a VERY good way.
BUT, the reason I cannot reccomend it right now is for two reasons.
Firstly, Denuvo + VMProtect are BOTH being used in this game to prevent it being cracked, but this has the downside of maxing out most peoples CPU's and crippling performance.
Even at a high resolution I am currently CPU bottlenecked where there is absolutely no reason for it to be. This is entirely because of Ubisoft's anti-consumer practices regarding DRM.
Seriously, Uplay + Steam + Denuvo + VMProtect, wtf
And secondly, the audio bugs. Right now I have to restart the game 3-4 times before I can play it. Sometimes it just kills my audio devices and I have to disable and re-enable them to make them work.
And sometimes it has an awful crackling the whole time. Not to mention the fact that the entire game is so damn quiet its ridiculous.
In regards to microtransactions, yes they are there, but not in any intrusive way.
I haven't felt the need to use them once as everything can be bought through normal play.
If the audio bugs are fixed, and Denuvo+VMProtect are removed then this would be a 100% reccomendation from me. The game itself is brilliant, its just being held back by anti-consumer practices.

I played this game thinking it would be more an interesting narrative and managing your own police force.  The narrative part is there as is the management but the management is what I ended up disliking in the end.
I thought I was going to have to deal with talking to my own officers and keeping their morale up or making an example out of them and demote them for stupid things, like coming in to work drunk.  Instead it is just a simple choice of firing them or promoting them in hopes he/she stops coming in intoxicated or constantly asking for a day off.
The calls in the game become boring about half way through the game.  Even if it sounds exciting, like a gun shooting, all you care about later in the game is if you have enough officers back in time to send out and just wishing the game day would end.
The investigation part of the game was a nice little puzzle to figure out but some of the clues/testimony/reports make it very confusing on how to picture everything together correctly.  I few of them I had to look up online because it was confusing on how to arrange what did happen.
The lack of randomization was another issue I did not like about the game.  If you wanted to play a day over because you lost some officers somewhere or your detectives screwed up with apprehending someone, just reload your game day.  Everything plays out exactly the same way except for who shows up for work or asks for the day off.
I very much disliked the political part of the game later on, with keeping officers happy by not sending them out with other officers who do not agree with their political choice.  I have to work with people who like/dislike President Donald Trump, I don't get to become unruly at work because I have to work with someone who disagrees with my political choice.  This should be the same with any police department.
Pointing out things I did like about the game, there is an interesting story dealing with Jack Boyd as he attempts to continue to stay in his position as Chief of Police all while looking for his wife and dealing with his drug problem.  He has to contend with a corrupt mayor and outside forces which wish to influence things in the city and especially with the police.
Not a bad game with an interesting story but the management part of the game needs some work to make it feel like there is progression in the game and not feel like it is just a big filler, a filler that made me decide to not recommend this game.

is a management sim on its face, an extremely narrative one. And before I get into it. I absolutely love what this game is going for but I have some serious criticisms about it. But I'll get to those later.
The setup is as such, you, the Chief of Police for the city of Freeburg named Jack Boyd is retiring in 180 days and desires to accumulate $500,000 in whatever way possible. Now, one of the main criticisms is that you cannot actually play as a good cop. You must at some level be corrupt. This is not really one of MY main critiques but I've heard many others complain about this. However, I believe it is inherent to have some amount of dealings with other, lets call them less than legal organizations for an authority to have any semblance of control over a large mass of people. Additionally, you are playing a character in a narratively driven game, not as yourself.
The main crux of this game is staring at a static 3D model of the scaled down city, and then responding and sending officers to calls. Each event is essentially a paragraph or two and you send an amount of officers and some support if desired such as SWAT and/or a paddy wagon. Which increase the success rate of your officers. It essentially operates with cooldowns and each call has a limited time to respond to; and its up to you to determine how many officers to send and whether or not a call even needs to be responded to.
Each call has different affects, sometimes the officers will call back to the station and ask what to do in certain situations or call for backup, in turn you decide to send more officers or not. These situations include multiple choice answers and selecting the right one will determine the success of your officers. More often than not, it relies on you having read and understood the situation at hand and dealing with it appropriately. For example, how to behave from the threat of violence as opposed to reacting to violence already committed all the way down to tricking a irate drug user or calmly walking up to someone deeply distraught.
There are a lot of systems in this game and they are all overlapping. I've heard complaints that they are heavily RNG-afied however they are very scripted and just have a high degree of learning to do to determine what is needed to not get your officers killed and still apprehend the offenders whilst being able to respond to the majority of calls.
There are detectives cases, and numerous affairs you must deal with. The game is split into 3 distinct chapters, you do not actually play all 180 days, otherwise the game would be 50 hours long. You'll deal with one major thing each chapter in addition to regular calls and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t from city hall trying to make your job much harder. For example: Serial killers,  Mafia Wars, Political protests rampant with racial and sexist tensions all the while trying to appease the Mayor and City Hall as to not get your budget cut as well as deal with personal issues with your officers such as alcoholism.
There are gangs to take down, reading profiles and doing interrogations, hiring snitches and finding workarounds for less than legal activities. The calls are color coded:
My main issue is that the game is so narrativley driven that it feels a little contrived at points, it at times feels so chaotic with little means to correct course that it becomes overbearing. However, I feel its purposefully contrived in this manner to fulfill the narrative. I once thought a not Jack Boyd version of running the station would be fun but I've, after finishing, decided that that would ultimately be too much of an undertaking and take away from the overall feeling.

כיאה למשחק שיצא בתחילת החודש, וחלה עליו הנחה יפה בחנות ה-STEAM, תפסתי את המשחק מהר כדי להשביע את הרעב שלי למשהו מרענן חוץ מ-Rocket League עטור השבחים וקאונטר סטרייק הישן והטוב. יחסית למשחק שנוצר בידי חבורת אלמונים, ולא ע"י חברת משחקים מוכרת, יש למשחק ריח מרענן מאוד. במשחק ישנה נטישה מוחלטת של הגרפיקות המציאותיות שרוקסטאר יוצרת עם GTA ויוביסופט עם FAR CRY, והמשחק כולו מעוצב בסגנון מיושן וארט-דקו. מסרטון הפתיחה - הגאוני בכל קנה מידה - אפשר להריח בקלות את מה שהמשחק רוצה שנרגיש.  הקול העבה והמרגיע של הדמות הראשית והומור גרוטסקי- מיני כבד מאוד אך לא מעיק או דוחה שקיים במשחק הוא בהחלט הישג של כותב טקסטים מחוכם ואינטיליגנט.
המשחק מספר את סיפורו של צ'יף המשטרה המקומי של העיר פרייבורג (Freeborg), ג'ק. לאחר שנקבע לג'ק תאריך פיטורים של 180 יום בתחילת המשחק אנו חיים את חיו כשוטר מסור בעיר מושחתת שבסך הכל מנסה לסיים את הקריירה שלו בתנאיו.
בדרכו של ג'ק עומדת המאפיה המקומית, ומאבק בינה אל מאפיונר חדש שמצטרף לעיר. לאחר מכן ישנו מאבק בין ה"מציל של העיר"- סוג של פיטר פן שחושף את עצמו לבין ראש העיר הוותיק והמושחת במאבק לראשות העירייה. ג'ק עומד באמצע כל המאבקים האלה כגיבור מקומי, צ'יף שתושבי העיר מעריצים והצד שג'ק בוחר בו, לרוב מנצח. המשחק מלא באפשרויות בחירה שישפיעו על המשחק, כך שניתן לשחק אותו מספר פעמים וליהנות ממשחק שונה למדי.
בנוסף לכל הריבים האלה אשתו של ג'ק עוזבת אותו במהלך המשחק, דבר שגורם לו לתהות רבות מתי תשוב לחייו, עד שנוצרת ידידות ואף יותר מכך עם התובעת העירונית החדשה. כמובן שגם פה יש לשחקן החלטות, המשפיעות גם על עתידו הזוגי של ג'ק במשחק.
המשחק עצמו מראה את עבודתו של ג'ק בניהול תחנת המשטרה, פיטור ומינוי שוטרים ושליחתם למשימות השונות המופיעות על גבי מפת העיר. המשחק מזכיר מאוד את המשחקים הדומים בקטגוריה ולא מראה שום חידוש כיאה למשחק דל תקציב. לעומת זאת, גדולתו של המשחק נמצאת דווקא בסצנות העלילה המתרחשות בין הימים שהשאירו אותי משתוקק לסוף היום כדי לראות מה מתרחש. בנוסף לכך, נהניתי מההומור הנפלא והגרפיקה שאישית משכה אותי מאוד, יחד עם מנגינות הסקסופון המהנות שהיוו אושר צרוף.
לסיכום, זהו משחק דל תקציב, דבר הניכר לעין, אך הוא בעל אוירה מרעננת וכיפית. העלילה מעניינת וההחלטות שעל השחקן לקחת הן גדולות וכך גם התוצאות וההשלכות שלהן על המשחק. יש למשחק מספר רב של סופים, חלקם מפתיעים וחלקם פחות בלשון המעטה. האוירה, המוזיקה, ההומור והגרפיקה עושים לי טעם של עוד. ציון 6.5

Okay.  I'm halfway through my third complete campaign.  At this point, I feel comfortable enough giving this game a thumbs down.
I love this game.  I think you will love this game.  It is a great game.  The plot is a thriller/espionage/mystery/cop drama that will suck you in and take you on an oxycodone rollercoaster of emotion.  It's so exciting, frustrating, funny and sad, and like a great book, you won't be able to put it down.
The plot is like GTAIV.  It is perfectly linear and every play through will present you with the exact same choices and challenges.  Only minute differences may occur depending on the two-option choices presented.
The biggest investigation of your carreer is a game error.  If you follow the linear plot and make the correct choices, you lose.  Check the forums, and you'll understand when you play yourself.  The final mission builds up to either a picture of victory or a picture of defeat.  No explanation or action, at all.  The only difference between the climax of your story and the mission where you arrest a woman for bathing in City Hall is the cutscene following the final mission.  It was disappointing.  Lastly, there was promise of a new gameplay mode, which would make up for the linear plot.  I might reverse my rating if it were ever to happen.
Edit:  I should've mentioned the amazing soundtrack.  It's amazing.  The beautiful selections may help you forget how disappointed you are.

Just finished Planetarian and thought I'd write a quick review for those considering it. I am not particularly into visual novels (I think this is the only one I've finished), so I can't really compare it to others. While the game feels padded with some unnecessary repetition at different points, it moved me like a video game hasn't moved me before. For some reason I can't explain, I really cared for the characters by the end (no, I'm not going to spoil anything). Part of it might the music, which I felt was superb.
Conclusion: I definitely recommend it if you are looking for a thought-provoking and emotional story. Be aware that it's a visual novel, so you make no choices and there is no "failure state." I'd also suggest doing it in one go (took me about four hours) for full effect.

Well, as someone who has never played (if you can call a "kinetic novel" playing) anything by Key before, I didn't quite know what was in store for me. It looked cute. There was a good deal. Why not? I didn't know I was going to end up crying. Multiple times. Set in a post-apocalyptic world, the narrator is a "Junker" who goes through old scrap to survive in a deadly world where other living people are few and far between and unlikely to be friendly. He encounters a robot who was left behind in a planetarium 30 years ago when the war broke out and who has no idea nobody is ever coming back for her or will ever visit the planetarium again. If that premise isn't depressing enough, it's all downhill from there. But was it worth it? Absolutely. Somehow the writers are able to pluck out just the right refrains to repeat, the right choice of words to tug at your proverbial heart strings at the right moments. Assuming you enjoy a sad story every now and again, this is absolutely worth your time.
An amazingingly sad and beautiful story that held my absolute attention the entire time. My all time favorite visual novel.

Apart from that it's just...go on your raft, travel from island to island, hunt down meat, and gather other materials to get better tools, which allow you to craft better clothes, which protect you better against the cold. Oh, there are also enemies on many maps, that seem to get more frequent the further you travel. You can kill those by either using poisoned meat (which means you're throwing away vital food for yourself) or with traps, which are next to impossible to set up when an enemy has already spotted you (and they spot you almost instantly) or use a bow, which requires several arrows for predators (3 for a ♥♥♥♥ing wolf), which in turn are hard to come by (after getting the bow and 9 arrows initially it took all of 2 islands to completely deplete my stack...then I died from a snake bite, which I shouldn't have even gotten in the first place...fun times).
The graphics are serviceable, the gameplay is ok, but the game imho is just too shallow and repetitive...a problem many survival games have. In the "story" you can return to a checkpoint when you die, but I just can't bring myself to repeat a section over and over again, because there's no incentive to do so. There's no narrative, nothing, so it's just another survival game in the end. Too bad. A lot of the issues could be fixed...like giving the player an option to sneak up on or avoid enemies entirely, instead of being spotted out of screen and making the bow actually useful for more than 2 or 3 stops...I think I didn't find any flint on the last 30 or so islands to even make new arrows...and then you need THREE to kill a wolf? Yes, yes, "git gud", but frankly, there's too little here to warrant to git gud.

Imagine Deus Ex combined with The Legend Of Zelda: A Link To The Past in a rogue-lite, and you'll end up roughly at Streets Of Rogue. The sheer number of classes is impressive, especially given that they tend to perform as described by the in-game text, in practice. And there'll be a create-a-class mode someday, which I'm quite excited about. And just like Deus Ex 2 (the really buggy, crashy one that everyone but me hated), you'll be able to interact in a very straightforward way with your surroundings and with the NPCs. Bribe guards, sneak around, hack terminals, shoot it out, punch it out, swords it out, recruit NPCs to fight with or for you, blow up the entire area, or chloroform the opposition one by one. This game's got all of that and more (somehow, in Early Access). And you won't be burdened by online-only singleplayer, microtransactions, extraneous DRM, requests for information, or its collection while playing Streets Of Rogue (as of 3/11/2017). It's hard to overemphasize just how much more fun I'm having with this game than I did Deus Ex Human Revolution (the game that convinced me to give up on Deus Ex as a series). Streets Of Rogue is a game that, in its current state and and along its apparent development trajectory, I very strongly recommend.

For Early Access, it shows quite a bit of potential. The missions so far are really basic (kill x number of NPCs and/or retrieve x number of items), but the tight controls and freedom given to the player makes up for it. It also has a wacky sense of humor that, if fully realized with 100% complete levels and co-op, can keep players hooked for hours. Think Miami Heat meets a Saints Row approach to sandbox gameplay: the more creative and obsurd you play, the more fun you'll have.
HOWEVER, right now the game is probably 25% complete. Characters and items are locked, and there are only two levels with 3 stages each for a total of 6 stages available. There is a hint of a story present, but it barely gets out of the introduction. Plus, the NPCs have typical filler dialogue that breaks the immersion (although this could be a design choice).
Overall, it's hard to justify buying this at Early Access, but once it's completed, it'd be worth the $15.

Using a post apocalyptic environment heavily influenced by the
movies, and a series of unlockable motorcycles and riders, you travel across the wastelands of the near future. Often fellow members of your biker gang will swing alongside you as you find yourself fending off attacks from rival gangs with lead pipes, Uzi machine guns and shining sabers, leaving behind crushed, decapitated and generally maimed motorcycles and bodies.
The storyline is rather basic but effective and really is a thin veil behind which lurks the true joy of this title - shunting along at increasingly ludicrous speeds will bashing the living sin out of pretty much all and sundry in your path. From errant police to monster trucks and huge hog riding brutes you bash and maul your way to victory.
The action is simple to learn and hard to master, one of my favorite things to say about any game. The difficulty ramps up smoothly and as you advance you get to unlock permanent stat boosts on every game death. Initially this might seem frustrating as you start at the very beginning each time - but it is not, as you always have a random mission objective and the tracks are proceduraly generated as you move across the map with the environment changing to show your progress. Furthermore, you unlock the ability to start at higher levels as well as gain bigger and more brash bikes and riders.
This is an excellent arcade game which is easily enjoyable and one of those you will keep coming back to for a quick session long after you have clocked it.

This game transcends its goal of being a road rash successor and is its own entertaining, violent, adrenaline-filled entity. From the colorful gangs, multitudes of weapons, stylish bikes and memorable racers, everything about Road Redemption is bursting with personality and high-octane adrenaline injectors. While the game might seem simple when you first load up the campaign, the increasing difficulty, track complexity and the ever-multiplying ways rival racers can cause you trouble soon turns the experience into a pulse-pounding challenge.
The skill tree, new bikes and upgrades you can purchase make things easier and more satisfying the more you play, but campaign+ and the brutal conditions imposed on the unlockable drivers soon correct the difficulty curve, so that mastering the game will prove a challenge to even the most seasoned gamer. It's one thing to beat campaign mode with the default driver, best bike and the full skill tree, but can you do it with a character who can't use guns? Or one who takes damage any time you use nitro? How about someoen with 1/4 the health as everyone else, or characters who don't get any benefits from the skill tree? Or how about a pacifist Santa Claus who can't damage enemies at all?
The game's procedural elements might seem a bit weak compared to something like Binding of Isaac, but there's just enough unpredictability in there to keep the game fresh even after you've cleared it several times.
This game isn't perfect though. There could be more gangs, and more environments, and more bosses, and more bikes, and more track variety, and more objectives. The soundtrack, while good, could use more tracks, and lacks a bit of personality compared to the licensed music from popular bands you might find in other similar games. But for a budget title made by a small team, these are flaws I can easily overlook. The story is a little bare bones, being conveyed largely through in-game dialogue (which thankfully doesn't get repetitive), and it'd be nice to have a little more information about the characters you play as and what motivates them. There's also the inherent frustration of the roguelite genre, where sometimes your skills are at the mercy of luck, and bad dice rolls force you into a Bad Run. The effectiveness of some weapons seems disproportionate to the ease with which you can acquire them. Finally, the difficulty might be a little too high for some people (I seriously doubt I'll ever clear the game with some of the more extreme drivers, and others' skill ceiling might manifest even sooner, unfortunately preventing them from experiencing a good chunk of the game's variety).
But for me, the good greatly outweighs the bad. At the time of this writing, the game is barely out of early access, so future updates might yet add more content or fix some of the flaws.
Bottom line: If killing people with pipes, swords, guns, hammers, bombs and grenade launchers while racing your bike at breakneck speed sounds like something you'd enjoy, this game is everything you want.
