What I am writing here is based on a true life story, 11 years ago in 2006 it was my first online game experience on GameSpy Arcade and I met someone that I had no idea she was a girl. We were talking for a while then when she gave me her MSN (If you are old enough you know what that is) I saw the photo I asked her if she is a girl she laughed and she said yes. I asked her name and it was "Emily".
After 3 months just talking on the internet one day she asked about my music taste and we had a very different music taste. But it was interesting for her (exactly like how it goes in this game). I was living in Iran by the time and she was from England. We had no way of seeing each other so all we could do was just to chat. She talked about her video games she liked Sims and Crash and I liked shooters and strategies. It truly was a shock for me but in this game one of the profile pictures you can take is "Company of Heroes" which was the game I was playing day and night back in 2006.
She spent a lot of time training my English and she was very successful. After a while I really started to feel for her although it was only internet. It even got to a point that I was dreaming that I was meeting her in person. She was very keeping in showing her emotions she was a very strong girl and very grown up in behaviour. We kept our connection for 7 years but it had up and downs.
In March 2014 we got in to a very bad argue over internet because of college she had moved to Germany and I was doing my best to go there I even learnt German but embassy rejected me just cause I was born in Iran although I even passed the German test which again was thanks to her help over internet teaching me German cause she was studying it. She started to be realistic saying this is going no where and we will never meet. I did not want to accept that I pushed it way too much that it really got scary for her and she ended all the connection ways by blocking me. I was very upset I had a pain in my heart that I really can't describe. I never had this feeling for any girl before although I had met them in person and not internet but I never ever did feel any pain like that night.
It took me a week to get over it. I started my swimming classes and I completely forgot about all of it. I am not sure how many of you played this game through "Emily" side but me and her had a nickname for each other and the nickname I chose for her 10 years ago does exist in this game with a little bit of different. I was calling her "Mimily" and she was calling me Prince of Persia.
4 months ago I came to Poland because for some reason I ended up being accepted to work for a video game company here in charge of MK X and Injustice for PC and many other games. One night I was walking in one of the streets in Warsaw and I saw this big hotel called "Marriott" which was Emily's surname. Believe me or not go to google and search it yourself, this hotel is located in a street called "Emili" and right on the other side of this hotel there is a small restaurant called "Prince of Persia". Can you imagine the feeling I had that night?
I dated many girls in these 4 years but none was something I could feel in my heart like I did with her. Every time I was reading a chat line in this video game it was like a sparkle of my past coming back to me. I feel like it was made for me, I have no idea how this is possible but if this is not miracle then what is it? Signs?
Thank you all for reading this, maybe I wrote too much off topic but I hope you understand how this game effected me and made me to type all these lines here.

Review in progress:
1. Looting. There's no "hold E" to loot for most of the items. You do have to hold it for the larger items, but that's not a big deal since it's faster than before and it's not all the time. +1 for me.
2. Game is beautiful. Draw distance is superb and adds to the realism. Characters are highly detailed.
3. Performance is really good (Very High settings at 1440p on a 1070 laptop 45-70 fps depending on the area. Desktop is 70-90 fps at very high 1440p 1080ti).  There's also a lot of PC specific settings, benchmarking, and in the options menu it'll tell you how the game ran for the past 30 seconds by giving you a graph with fps and frametime for CPU and GPU.
4. In terms of gear, you can obviously gain loot from high ranking captains and such, but you if you find a certain sword or bow that you like, you can go to a blacksmith and upgrade your weapon and it'll scale to your level.
5. No Chromatic abberation, film grain, vignetting, or motion blur. +4 for me.
6.I like that you have a mount.
7. You have a more control over your parkour. In previous games I got annoyed at times because my character would run up a wrong wall or do something that I didn't want them to do. So far, this version seems to be more fluid. While I'm talking about parkour, it doesn't play as significant of a role as previous games. Which is fine by me. It's fun, but it did become monotonous in the other titles.
8. Combat system does take some getting used to
9. There is auto-movement (like using the jeep in FC4), which is nice so you can enjoy the scenery. You can create custom markers to auto travel to;  you're not limited to objectives.
10. Side missions are much, much better than before. Granted I haven't played them all and they may end up becoming repetitive, but they feel a lot like the Witcher 3's side quests. Now, they're no where near as good as the Witcher (I mean, the Baron's side quests were some of the best I've ever played), but for Ubisoft to take some time and flesh them out, add variety, fully voice act a lot of them shows they're trying to make a change. In the previous AC games, I rarely did the side missions. They felt so boring, repetitive, and completely forgetable.
11. The world feels alive. Black Flag and Unity were excellent in creating the world that felt alive and bustling. Syndicate felt dead. I think they took another cue from Witcher here.
12. I like the main character a lot. I think the voice actor did a great job. But a lot of times the mocap seems off with his lips...Not ME:A bad, just not as good as it could be.
It feels like they took a few of the better ideas from other successful games while maintaining the AC identity. Glad I bought it. I was skeptical at first because Ubisoft has a way of making games look and play better than they actually are, but I think this one is a good and much needed change for the series. There are a lot of things in the open world that are useless and are simply clutter, but I think the new changes make the game a much better entry to the series than the stagnant yearly release it was in before. I'll be updating the review once I'm finished with the game to discuss story/characters.

I do love a good trivia game. But I like even more when there's lots of twists, nooks and crannies to spice up the gameplay. And this game is no exception. The 4th installment of the You Don't Know Jack trivia game series brings us more than we have seen in any of the games so far. You get to experience new things like Screws that can fly onto the screen and block the question and answers. Another new feature is the game categories, the new ones specifically. Each of which do a spectacular job of heightening up the facts as well as making your brain go numb about what the next answer could be.  Take Roadkill for example, a game with 7 answers followed by a final bonus which tips the scales in any way. Get the first few answers right and you're good to go. Get the final bonus wrong however and you can kiss your cash goodbye!
I also like the fact that you can get different amounts of cash when you buzz in to pick an amount. From the stingy $120 up to $12,000 in one question. However depending on the difficulty of the question the maximum value goes up and down. And that helps when thinking whether to relax or not.
Another great feature is that all your favourite characters are there; Cookie, Guy, Schmitty, Buzz and Nate, all of whom get to play a decent role in the game.
YDKJ 4 (The Ride) has some great things to offer. I can't really fit it all in, so I suggest you play it to find out more.
